### 24.91.1 Placement and invocation invariants

1. Put model-typed ports beside authentic models under `legado-runtime/src/main/kotlin/io/legado/runtime/host/`. Keep generic UI/browser/verification/coroutine contracts in `:integration-contract`; `:legado-runtime` may depend on `:integration-contract` and `:legado-rhino`, never `:app`; `:app` implements the ports. Do not import Legado model types into the Kotlin/JVM contract module.
2. Keep caller-specific `java` ownership: BaseSource direct eval binds `java/source/sourceApi` to the same BaseSource; AnalyzeRule eval binds `java` to AnalyzeRule and `source` to BaseSource; payAction/image-click/callBackJs/legacy login use SourceLoginJsExtensions-compatible `java`; Login UI v2 is separate; WebView page RPC is not normal Rhino execution.
3. The invocation envelope carries `SourceExecutionContext`, caller kind, authentic BaseSource, optional live Book/BookChapter/list, nullable caller values, base URL/key/page and raw `result` only where the pinned caller supplies it. Keep Book/BookChapter typed. `Any?` is retained only for raw JS result/return values where upstream itself uses it, never as a replacement source-model bridge.

### 24.91.2 Proposed signatures — design sketch only

```kotlin
interface LegadoRuntimeHost {
    val catalog: BookSourceCatalogPort
    val sourceState: SourceExecutionStatePort
    val explore: ExploreCatalogPort
    val sourceVariables: SourceVariablePort
    val ruleVariables: RuleVariablePort
    val sessions: SourceSessionPort
    val cookies: SourceCookiePort
    val cache: SourceCachePort
    val http: SourceHttpPort
    val images: SourceImageTransportPort
    val actions: SourceActionPort
    val replacements: ReplacementRuntimePort
}

interface BookSourceCatalogPort {
    suspend fun find(bookSourceUrl: String): BookSource?
    suspend fun listForExecution(): List<BookSource>
    suspend fun insertReplace(sources: List<BookSource>, origin: SourceMutationOrigin, batch: SourceBatchPolicy): SourceMutationReceipt
    suspend fun update(source: BookSource, origin: SourceMutationOrigin): SourceUpdateReceipt
    suspend fun delete(bookSourceUrls: List<String>, origin: SourceMutationOrigin): SourceDeleteReceipt
}

interface SourceExecutionStatePort {
    fun invalidateSourceGlobals(sourceClass: Class<out BaseSource>, sourceKey: String)
    suspend fun removeSharedLibrary(jsLib: String?)
    suspend fun removeSourceConfig(sourceKey: String)
    fun clearSourceVariableMemory(sourceKey: String)
    suspend fun resetConcurrentRate(sourceKey: String)
}

interface ExploreCatalogPort {
    suspend fun <T> withSourceLock(sourceUrl: String, block: suspend () -> T): T
    suspend fun getResult(sourceUrl: String, exploreUrl: String): String?
    suspend fun putResult(sourceUrl: String, exploreUrl: String, rawResult: String)
    suspend fun clearResult(sourceUrl: String, exploreUrl: String)
    fun acquireInfoMap(sourceUrl: String): InfoMap
    suspend fun persistInfoMap(sourceUrl: String)
    fun invalidateInfoMap(sourceUrl: String, reason: SourceStateInvalidationReason)
}

interface SourceVariablePort {
    fun getVariable(sourceKey: String): String
    fun putVariable(sourceKey: String, value: String?)
    fun get(sourceKey: String, key: String): String
    fun put(sourceKey: String, key: String, value: String)
}

interface RuleVariablePort {
    fun getBookVariable(bookUrl: String, key: String): String?
    fun putBookVariable(bookUrl: String, key: String, value: String?)
    fun getChapterVariable(bookUrl: String, chapterUrl: String, key: String): String?
    fun putChapterVariable(bookUrl: String, chapterUrl: String, key: String, value: String?)
    suspend fun clearInvalidBookValues(existingBookUrls: Set<String>)
}

interface SourceSessionPort {
    fun getLoginHeader(sourceKey: String): String?
    fun putLoginHeader(sourceKey: String, headerJson: String)
    fun removeLoginHeader(sourceKey: String)
    fun getLoginInfo(sourceKey: String): String?
    fun putLoginInfo(sourceKey: String, infoJson: String)
    fun removeLoginInfo(sourceKey: String)
}

interface SourceCookiePort {
    fun getCookie(url: String): String
    fun getKey(): String
    fun setCookie(url: String, cookie: String)
    fun replaceCookie(url: String, cookie: String)
    fun removeCookie(url: String)
    fun removeCookie(url: String, key: String)
    suspend fun setWebCookie(url: String, cookie: String): HostPortResult<Unit>
}

interface SourceHttpPort { suspend fun execute(request: RuntimeHttpRequest): RuntimeHttpResponse }
interface SourceImageTransportPort { suspend fun fetch(request: SourceImageRequest): SourceImageResponse }
interface SourceActionPort {
    suspend fun dispatch(action: SourceHostAction, context: SourceExecutionContext): HostPortResult<SourceActionResult>
    suspend fun upLoginData(data: Map<String, Any?>?): HostPortResult<Unit>
    suspend fun reLoginView(context: SourceExecutionContext): HostPortResult<Unit>
}
interface ReplacementRuntimePort {
    suspend fun disable(rule: ReplaceRule, reason: ReplacementDisableReason): HostPortResult<Unit>
    suspend fun reportTimeout(ruleName: String, detail: String): HostPortResult<ReplacementTimeoutDisposition>
}
```

**Semantics that signatures must preserve**

- `SourceMutationOrigin` distinguishes edit UI, JS upsert, MCP declarative, manual import, RuleUpdate subscription, HTTP JSON single/batch, legacy import, backup restore, management metadata and delete. `SourceBatchPolicy` distinguishes one Room transaction from per-item partial acceptance. Receipts report per-item accepted/rejected and check-state reset without claiming cross-store atomicity.
- DAO insert is transactional REPLACE + check-state reset. Full update resets check state only when `checkContent()` changes; it normalizes order/enabled/explore-enabled/update-time/respond-time/weight, while group-only changes can reset state. Narrow metadata SQL methods remain narrow.
- Delete preserves source-row + persisted source-variable deletion in one transaction; source-key shared-global invalidation occurs before delete, SourceConfig and generic in-memory variable cleanup after commit. Do not claim production deletion evicts the Explore InfoMap object LRU.
- Source-key shared-global invalidation (`sourceClass.name + MD5(sourceKey)`) is distinct from jsLib-hash-wide scope/file/global invalidation. The latter may affect several source URLs. Neither proves cancellation of scripts already running.
- Explore result key is `MD5(sourceUrl + exploreUrl)`; preserve persistent `ACache('explore')`, process-memory results, source-scoped serialization and stable mutable `InfoMap(sourceUrl)` identity. Clearing results must not evict InfoMap. Its persistent key, generic memory entry and separate object LRU are separate state layers.
- `sourceVariable_<sourceKey>` is distinct from `v_<sourceKey>_<key>`. RuleData big-value backing preserves the 10,000-character inline threshold in `RuleDataInterface`, null deletion, empty fallback, MD5(bookUrl/chapterUrl/key), `bookUrl.txt`, synchronized access and invalid-book cleanup. RSS variables remain separate.
- Login header/info storage is separate from CookieStore. Cookie operations preserve domain/merge/enable semantics and WebView CookieManager synchronization. Cache operations separately preserve text/file/memory, `onlyDisk`, TTL seconds and byte-array/large-file behavior.
- New `RuntimeHttpRequest/Response` and `SourceImageRequest/Response` must preserve source identity, URL/options, method/body, multi-value headers, timeout/retry/redirect, cookie-jar choice, status/final URL, bytes or closeable stream, cancellation, close and error. Runtime owns AnalyzeUrl/source-specific cover/chapter decode; host owns OkHttp/Glide DataFetcher and presentation.
- Reuse existing `HostUiPort`, `HiddenWebViewPort`, `VisibleBrowserPort`, `VerificationCodePort` and `ProductEventPort`; add typed login callbacks with main-thread ordering, lifecycle cancellation and exactly-once completion. `WebJsExtensions.request/upConfig` page RPC remains a separate WebView owner.
- Regex execution for `BookChapter.getDisplayTitle`/`ContentProcessor` remains in Runtime; timeout prompt, crash persistence, rule-disable DAO and restart policy are host ports. Source-import replacement, editor preview and ReplaceRuleController retain separate caller paths.

### 24.91.3 Caller-specific mutation policy — no universal upsert

| Origin | Pinned write semantics | Port requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Manual import / RuleUpdate | SourceHelp 18+ filter, transactional REPLACE/check reset, async order normalization; no edit/upsert cleanup | Preserve this origin policy; do not route through delete helper |
| HTTP JSON single | Nonblank name/URL validation then direct DAO REPLACE; no 18+ filter | No implicit JS-upsert invalidation |
| HTTP JSON batch | Per-item direct inserts; partial accepted subset | Preserve per-item transaction and partial result |
| Legacy import / backup restore | Parse/deserialise then direct DAO REPLACE | Preserve conversion path and no inferred cleanup |
| Edit / JS upsert / MCP | Explicit old/new comparison and distinct Explore/jsLib/SourceConfig/concurrent-rate ordering | Preserve each origin; URL change is delete-old + insert-new with conflict checks |
| DAO update / metadata | Full update checkContent comparison; narrow SQL metadata methods | Preserve both paths |
| Delete | SourceHelp row + persisted variables transaction; source globals before, SourceConfig/memory cleanup after | Preserve ordering; do not imply InfoMap eviction |

A wrapper cannot subclass the final data class, and moving BaseSource as-is leaks App side effects. No typed per-source delegate that preserves JS API, self identity, lifecycle and concurrency has yet been proven. **Do not copy BookSource alone or use a global service locator/ThreadLocal shortcut.** All 29 methods and effects are recorded in `basesource-host-methods.tsv`.

Current DTO equality is data-class all-fields equality, so catalog invalidation must not reuse it as upstream equality.
- **Room boundary:** upstream AppDatabase is Room version 113 with BookSource, BookSourceCheckState and BookSourcePart view among many unrelated product entities. `BookSourceDao.insert` is transactional with REPLACE and check-state save; `update` resets check state only when `checkContent()` differs; delete cascades check state; DAO also exposes enable/enableExplore/order/group/search/list flows. These remain App host/catalog concerns. `:legado-runtime` already applies Parcelize 2.4.20; `room-common:2.8.4` may be sufficient for entity annotations if needed, but no Room runtime/compiler/KSP/AppDatabase/schema v1 is authorized. `BaseBook` is a separate book model, not a parent of BookSource.

Current catalog lacks upstream DAO operations such as enableExplore, group/order, search/filter and check-state flows. Do not move AtomicFile/Context/DAO into Runtime.

## 24.135 Task 026Q result — public synthetic sidecar API rejected by pinned Rhino

- **Identity:** Task 026Q registered at HEAD 51e7a9a0994d2b42b9b34a39eb0f29a647394db5; review HEAD before this result record 83b1c651447d30b348055cc7680ddcee5698b220; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a. Probe source/classes/dumps/logs are outside the repository at /tmp/task026q-sidecar-probe/; result record SHA-256 is in RESULT.sha256.
- **Cross-module Kotlin:** separate Runtime and App consumer modules compiled with cached Kotlin 2.4.20. App consumer successfully called public @JvmSynthetic attach/read methods.
- **JVM/Java reflection:** interface and implementation methods are ACC_PUBLIC | ACC_SYNTHETIC; Java reflection returns both and reports isSynthetic() == true. The internal-member negative consumer compile fails as expected; its JVM method is public, mangled and non-synthetic, so internal is not a viable App source API.
- **Decisive Rhino result:** used the exact pinned HtmlUnit CoreJS 5.3.0-legado.4 JAR and pinned upstream modules/rhino Debug classes JAR, with the actual RhinoWrapFactory/CatchableNativeJavaObject path. Rhino JS reports function|function|function for the two synthetic owner methods and an ordinary method. The pinned JavaMembers bytecode collects public/protected methods through getDeclaredMethods/getMethods and has no Method.isSynthetic filter; RhinoClassShutter is class-level, not member-level. **Public @JvmSynthetic methods are therefore script-visible and rejected for attachment on BookSource.**
- **Serialization mechanism:** the minimal body-property sidecar is private transient and has Room Ignore in classfile RuntimeInvisibleAnnotations. Gson omits it. Parcelize-generated writeToParcel writes only the primary constructor properties. Data-class copy does not copy the body sidecar; equals/hashCode ignore it. Java reflection cannot see Room Ignore because its retention is BINARY; javap confirms placement. Actual Android Parcel roundtrip and Room processor/schema were not run.
- **Scope limit:** this was a minimal BookSourceProbe, not real BookSource/BaseSource. Real field/copy/import/restore/Room/Parcelable behavior and every BaseSource implementer remain unproven. No production code or build file changed.
- **Disposition:** 026Q complete for the bounded mechanism probe. The public synthetic per-source owner method is rejected with the current Rhino wrapper. A method-level Rhino hiding mechanism or another non-reflective attachment design must be separately designed and proven before migration. Body-property transient/Ignore/IgnoredOnParcel remains a candidate only if explicit reattachment after copy/import/restore is proven on real BookSource.
- **No execution expansion:** no Gradle task, App compile, build/test, Room KSP, DEX/R8, CI/device/network or production migration. Phase A remains open; Task 027 blocked; Stage-0 in_progress/not accepted; Stage-1 **NO-GO**; full compatibility **NOT ESTABLISHED**.
- **Next:** register a bounded read-only Rhino member-filter feasibility probe. Do not edit production Rhino or Runtime code in that probe.

## 24.137 Task 026R result — method-level Rhino host-member filter is feasible under unique-name constraint

- **Identity:** Task 026R registered at HEAD a7d5b71ba798687355a0a1bf975536c7836c33e4; review HEAD before result record 0b00641d637cdb40163e9277885a0e054a630a19; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a. Scratch evidence and result hash are under /tmp/task026r-rhino-filter-probe/.
- **Interception point:** pinned CatchableNativeJavaObject is open and its get method is overridable. It currently wraps super.get() through CatchableJavaMethodCache and catchJavaInvocation. A scratch subclass can check a runtime-retained method marker before super.get(), and also override has/getIds.
- **Positive result:** actual pinned RhinoWrapFactory-compatible scratch wrapper plus the exact pinned Rhino classes/HtmlUnit CoreJS hides unique marked methods: direct property is undefined; in and hasOwnProperty are false; Object.keys does not list them. A marked superclass method and marked interface-default method are also hidden. Ordinary getKey/getTag/ordinaryMethod remain callable. Separate App Kotlin consumer can still call the @JvmSynthetic host methods; output hostSide=host-token|hidden-interface.
- **Overload limitation:** when a name has both a marked Int overload and an unmarked String overload, the safe filter fails open and exposes both. Therefore host-only attachment/accessor method names must be reserved, unique and non-overloaded; never share a method name with an existing script API. This is an explicit contract constraint, not a passing mixed-overload filter.
- **Filter contract:** method-level runtime-retained annotation with FUNCTION target; define it in :legado-rhino (or a neutral module both sides can depend on), because Runtime depends on Rhino and Rhino must not depend on Runtime. Mark concrete implementations/overrides. Hide only when all public methods with that name are marked. Override get, has and getIds. Keep @JvmSynthetic for Java-source visibility; it is not itself the Rhino filter.
- **Compatibility boundary:** scratch factory exercised the ordinary object path only. Production integration must preserve RhinoWrapFactory.wrapOrNull special factories and NativeJavaList/Map/Array paths. It does not prove all 77 upstream APIs, real BookSource/all BaseSource implementers, R8 annotation retention, performance or dynamic App behavior.
- **Disposition:** 026R complete as bounded scratch feasibility. A method-level Rhino marker filter is a viable candidate only under the unique-name/no-overload rule; no production change is authorized by this result. Phase A remains open; Task 027 blocked; Stage-0 in_progress/not accepted; Stage-1 **NO-GO**; full compatibility **NOT ESTABLISHED**.
- **No execution expansion:** no tracked source/build/test/Gradle/workflow/schema/UI/Reader edit, no App compile/build/test, DEX/R8, CI/device/network or production Rhino/Runtime edit.
- **Next:** register a read-only inventory of all BookSource copy/creation/Room/Parcelable/Gson/import/restore paths and all BaseSource implementer attachment sites. Determine every place that must attach/re-attach the same per-source Host Services object before any implementation task.

## 24.147 Task 026W result — R8 marker annotation retention and name-collision feasibility

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-R8-HOST-MARKER-RETENTION-PROBE-026W; bounded scratch R8 probe complete, no production changes.
- **Registration start HEAD:** 6141b1f7ffb55246468d81b6247ef88ae77c3aaa. **Execution HEAD:** 055cad276279c3b0eaa165b64dcf9c9297285caa. Branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a.
- **Evidence:** /tmp/task026w-r8-marker-probe/RESULT.md SHA-256 95939c1f1f2fa874e1be8e3a02bd60dfb087d2ce7a415dbafebafab533444515; HASHES.txt SHA-256 966bbfb80b2c321655a0cc7bd3789fcb8c2153b6609ff6b68af28755702a9976; R8 input JAR SHA-256 9a7d1e9e4c2d3ee05482b9695df5f4d8f92c22ebb74603d6be4eab0505467f1a.
- **Tool:** cached R8 9.1.29 build 7130940ccb0c41990c77906b3d4f0a4412acb501. Three classfile Release scratch runs and two collision runs exited 0; no Gradle invocation.
- **Case A:** keeping the annotation interface but omitting keepattributes removed RuntimeVisibleAnnotations from host methods. Runtime reflection found no RhinoHostOnly marker on BookSourceProbe methods. Annotation class retention alone is insufficient.
- **Case B:** adding -keepattributes *Annotation* preserved the runtime marker, but allowing method obfuscation renamed host-only and ordinary methods into the same names. In BookSourceProbe, method name groups included both marked and unmarked methods. In a dedicated collision class, attachHostServices(HostServicesProbe) and nine ordinary methods with different descriptors all became method name a; reflection confirmed one marked plus nine unmarked methods in that same name group. The current name-based fail-open filter would expose the host-only method.
- **Case C:** adding the marker-specific rule -keepclassmembers class * { @com.script.rhino.RhinoHostOnly <methods>; } preserved marker method names while ordinary methods remained obfuscatable. attachHostServices/requireHostServices stayed named and annotated on the interface, concrete class and Kotlin-generated delegation proxy. The collision class kept attachHostServices distinct while ordinary methods became a.
- **Candidate minimal marker rules:** keep RuntimeVisibleAnnotations (*Annotation*), keep the RhinoHostOnly annotation type, and keep the names of methods annotated with RhinoHostOnly using the marker-specific keepclassmembers rule above. This is a candidate for module consumer rules, not yet validated in the actual Badcat Release dependency graph.
- **Important:** marker metadata retention alone is not enough. Because Rhino resolves a JavaScript property by name, method-name collisions after R8 create a mixed overload group; fail-open then leaks the marked method. Keep marker-bearing names or redesign the exposure contract before any production integration.
- **Limits:** scratch classes only; broad test keep rules intentionally kept classes/members while permitting obfuscation. R8 emitted informational duplicate-definition notices because modified scratch Rhino classes were program inputs while the pinned Rhino JAR was also a library. No actual Badcat Gradle Release/R8/DEX/APK run, no App ABI, no real BookSource/RssSource/HttpTTS/CoverRule, no Room/Gson/Parcelize, no CI/device/network.
- **Disposition:** Task 026W complete as bounded R8 feasibility evidence. Actual Badcat Release marker retention and App ABI remain NOT ESTABLISHED. Phase A remains open; broad BookSource/BaseSource Phase B migration blocked; Task 027 blocked; Stage-0 in_progress/not accepted; Stage-1 **NO-GO**; full Legado compatibility **NOT ESTABLISHED**.
- **Next:** continue independent Phase A actual App ABI/Release R8 and real Android lifecycle gates. Do not treat this scratch result as release proof or begin production marker/sidecar changes.

## 24.154 Task 026Z result — SharedJsScope is Runtime-owned; no same-source execution mutex

- **Task:** `R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-SHARED-JS-SCOPE-EXECUTION-STATE-PORT-CLOSURE-026Z`; complete for static source/caller/ownership and existing Release DEX reconciliation only. Registration HEAD `2578baba73e3386a204a117148bdd4ce92f68681`; execution source HEAD `2a2f6eb64fa8473bc15be07651c9cc7d6d4999df`; pinned upstream `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Decision 1 — no SharedJsScopePort:** upstream SharedJsScope scope creation, weak/LRU caching, per-key creation locks, CryptoJS owner/thread scopes, jsLib parent scopes, ScriptBindings shared-global handles/generations and invalidation are Runtime/Rhino execution semantics. Keep the manager Runtime-owned; do not expose an App-facing SharedJsScopePort. The current file is not portable as-is because it calls App asset, OkHttp, ACache, Debug and AppLog facilities. Those side effects need narrow typed adapters (CryptoJS asset, shared-library fetch, shared-library persistent cache, diagnostics); existing generic Resource/HTTP/Cache port rows are not yet proven semantically equivalent.
- **Decision 2 — reject same-source execution mutex as upstream contract:** BaseSource.evalJS, JsSourceEngine, AnalyzeRule and AnalyzeUrl each create fresh ScriptBindings/VarScope per invocation. The cached jsLib scope is the shared parent; source-specific `globalThis/global` is a generation-keyed ConcurrentNativeObject identified by `MD5(jsLib):javaClass.name:MD5(getKey())`. There is no global lock around all scripts from one source. `SourceLock.singleFlight/lock/tick` are explicit named JS APIs keyed by source key plus caller name; ConcurrentRateLimiter gates HTTP request cadence, not JS evaluation. Do not implement SourceExecutionStatePort as a same-source mutex or persistent per-source ScriptBindings.
- **Exact scope behavior:** SharedJsScope custom-library cache is LRU 16 + WeakReference keyed by MD5(jsLib), with a per-key creation monitor; different libraries can initialize concurrently. CryptoJS compiled script is process-cached; CryptoJS scopes are keyed by owner object identity + current Thread identity. `remove(jsLib)` removes the library's absolute-URL ACache entries, evicts that shared library scope and invalidates every shared-global state with the library-hash prefix. Source-key invalidation is separately keyed by concrete source class + MD5(getKey()) across library versions. Generation invalidation does not cancel already-running scripts.
- **Invocation identities:** BaseSource.evalJS binds `java = source = sourceApi = this`; JsSourceEngine binds `java = JsSourceEngine` and `source = sourceApi = BookSource`; AnalyzeRule and AnalyzeUrl have their own `java` object and per-call bindings. JsSourceConfig extraction has no BaseSource and only installs CryptoJS. A single attached BaseSource sidecar can service source-bound host effects across these paths, but it must not flatten their invocation-specific JS binding identities or CoroutineContext.
- **Badcat delta:** current RhinoSourceScriptRuntime uses process-static sourceId-keyed maps and Mutexes; it serializes evaluate/getString/putString/clear for one source, retains one ScriptBindings/VarScope across requests, evaluates jsLib/mainJs once in that persistent scope, and invalidates both when either hash changes. Upstream instead creates fresh invocation scopes and shares the library parent/global object separately. Badcat's global key `badcat-source:<sourceId>` also omits the upstream library hash and concrete BaseSource class. These are real semantic differences, not an injectable-interface naming issue.
- **Lifecycle correction:** current production SourceScriptRuntime exposes evaluate/getString/putString only; no SourceExecutionStatePort or SharedJsScopePort exists in production. clearSourceState is a concrete RhinoSourceScriptRuntime method. FileBookSourceCatalog defaults its invalidation callback to no-op; SourceCatalogActivity constructs a separate runtime and explicitly wires it, while BadcatReadingEngineFactory's catalog uses the no-op default. This is not one central lifecycle owner. Sidecar attachment and source/library invalidation must be separate from the Runtime-owned scope manager; exact public signatures remain unfrozen.
- **Host side effects:** CryptoJS asset comes from `appCtx.assets/scripts/cryptojs.min.js`; remote jsLib uses source-less global OkHttp with zero retries and cancellation-aware callback await plus BOM/charset/EncodingDetect text decoding; downloaded text is cached by MD5(URL) in ACache under `cacheDir/shareJs`, 50 MiB max and no expiry for the calls used here; failures use Debug/AppLog. `SharedJsScope.getScope` wraps the fetch in runBlocking without passing its caller CoroutineContext. Exact adapters and cancellation contract remain open.
- **Source/test/DEX evidence:** full line-backed map and limitations are in `/tmp/task026z-shared-scope-port/RESULT.md` SHA-256 `1e92a7b73cbc4e6a4118435359f8e05af2c65ba8827e9b35dee38ea84e5b33f4`; source/evidence hashes are in `SOURCE-HASHES.txt`. Pinned upstream test declarations cover source-specific invalidation, stale handles, concurrent global writes, owner/thread crypto isolation and per-library concurrent initialization, but none were executed by this task. Existing exact-pinned Release DEX `JsSourceEngine.smali.txt` SHA-256 `5e5ddd5752a305849cc94121e89a7e63b9c18c869d0cee35d997d2d80502f628` corroborates a fresh ScriptBindings allocation and per-call mainJs evaluation; `BaseSourceDefaultImpls.smali.txt` SHA-256 `4210cb0df081902ca9dc47207a8d217e4df35d37ad236bfc00223fedacf8bed4` corroborates BaseSource binding identity. SharedJsScope itself is R8-obfuscated and no mapping was uploaded.
- **No execution claim:** static source/caller review and previously recovered Release DEX only; no build/compiler/test/dependency resolution/DEX/R8/CI/device/network run and no production changes.
- **Disposition:** Task 026Z complete for static caller/ownership closure. Phase A remains open; broad BookSource/BaseSource migration blocked; Task 027 blocked; Stage-0 `in_progress / not accepted`; Stage-1 **NO-GO**; full compatibility **NOT ESTABLISHED**. Task 026M remains the only bounded Phase B implementation slice.
- **Next:** before any sidecar/scope implementation, freeze the exact App resource/fetch/cache/diagnostic adapters and a separate same-object sidecar attach + source/library invalidation lifecycle API; preserve fresh per-call ScriptBindings and upstream concurrency semantics. ## 24.156 Task 026AA result — exact SharedJsScope host dependencies and BaseSource lifecycle boundary

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-SHARED-LIBRARY-HOST-ADAPTER-AND-SOURCE-LIFECYCLE-CONTRACT-026AA; complete for static host-adapter and source-lifecycle contract closure only. - **CryptoJS asset:** SharedJsScope reads assets/scripts/cryptojs.min.js via appCtx AssetManager bufferedReader/readText (UTF-8); asset is 64,234 bytes, SHA-256 f40d295487ace92c3cc8e15eb32baa1ded2610da5bff7e955f40e748985c9701. Text and compiled Rhino script are separately process-cached. Load Exception is caught; Debug.log and AppLog.putDebug are best-effort; load returns null. Candidate typed adapter is a Runtime asset-text reader; do not pass Android Context/AssetManager into Runtime.
- **Exact shared-library HTTP:** SharedJsScope builds a URL-only GET request with no sourceId, source headers, CookieJar header or source cookie context. newCallStrResponse uses retry=0; response status is not checked and only body text is consumed. Text strips UTF-8 BOM, honors Content-Type charset, else EncodingDetect. Call.await cancels OkHttp Call on coroutine cancellation, but SharedJsScope wraps it in a fresh runBlocking without caller CoroutineContext, so parent source cancellation is not propagated. Global client has 15s connect/write, 60s read/call, connection retry true, ordinary and SSL redirects true, MODERN/COMPATIBLE/CLEARTEXT specs, trust-all SSL manager and hostname verifier, dynamic AppConfig UA/address DNS, keep-alive/cache-control headers, optional Cronet interceptor, HTTP logging and transparent gzip/deflate/br decompression. CookieJar builder registration is commented out; CookieManager network interceptor only runs with an internal CookieJar request header that this URL-only request does not set.
- **Security stop:** Badcat's current SourceRequestClient is intentionally source-scoped and safer: sourceId mandatory, source-cookie jar by default, strict URL/credential/header validation, 8 MiB request/response bounds, 20/45/30s connect/read/write, 60s call, ordinary redirects true but HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects false. It returns typed HTTP status/body and has retry policy; it is not equivalent to the upstream global client. Do not reuse it as-is or weaken it globally. Exact legacy trust-all TLS/HTTPS-downgrade compatibility requires a separate product/security decision; no TLS policy is frozen here.
- **Shared-library cache:** appCtx.cacheDir/shareJs, ACache process singleton, logical key MD5(URL), physical filename Java String.hashCode of that key, max size 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB), max count Int.MAX_VALUE, LRU by last access/lastModified, no TTL for SharedJsScope's put(key,value) calls. ACache remove returns Boolean but caller ignores it. SourceScriptFileCacheStore is sourceId/key namespaced, SHA-256/AtomicFile, 50 MiB budget and a different directory; it is not a direct substitute. A dedicated SharedLibraryCachePort is needed; a lower-level implementation may be reused only behind a dedicated namespace and exact capacity/policy.
- **Diagnostics:** Debug.log uses current source-debug callback and BuildConfig.DEBUG Logcat; AppLog.putDebug is recordLog-gated, keeps an in-memory 100-entry list and posts APP_LOG_UPDATED; HttpLogInterceptor is separately recordHttpLog-gated and redacts URL/headers with 8 KiB body capture. A single println/logger is not equivalent; no production diagnostics port exists.
- **Current port inventory:** RuntimeHostPort declares only HiddenWebViewPort, VisibleBrowserPort, VerificationCodePort, HostUiPort and ProductEventPort. No Resource/Asset, SharedLibraryHttp, SharedLibraryCache, RuntimeDiagnostics, SharedJsScope or SourceExecutionState port/owner exists in production source. SourceRequestClient, SourceScriptFileCacheStore and SourceScriptKeyValueStore have distinct source-scoped contracts and cannot be reused as-is for SharedJsScope.

AnalyzeRule and AnalyzeUrl bind java to themselves and source to the optional BaseSource, with no sourceApi alias. SourceLoginJsExtensions and WebJsExtensions are separate host objects. Null-source AnalyzeRule/AnalyzeUrl and JsSourceConfig have no BaseSource sidecar and must retain CryptoJS fallback.

SourceLoginUiV2Activity and SourceCatalogActivity construct separate RhinoSourceScriptRuntime instances. LegadoSourceLoginUiV2Service and RhinoEmbeddedUrlScriptEvaluator have default independent runtime construction; BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory also has a default runtime when not injected (factory currently passes its active runtime). ## 24.176 Task 026AK result — source image decode, Glide/Media3 and AppCompat lifecycle classified

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-IMAGE-MEDIA-APPCOMPAT-LIFECYCLE-CLOSURE-026AK; bounded read-only caller/owner classification complete. Registration start HEAD b3da915da7fa81e950e0c3e796fd3acd437cb4d6; registration/execution HEAD 8bd48539fb52d55990a9b6a2535d62902b55a547; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a.
- **Image decode runtime:** `ImageUtils.decode` selects `BookSource.coverDecodeJs` for covers and `ContentRule.imageDecode` for content/manga images; it evaluates source JS through `BaseSource.evalJS` with `book`, `result` and `src` bindings. Empty rule returns original data; failure logs via AppLog and returns null. `ImageUtils.skipDecode` checks the same selected rule. `RssSource.coverDecodeJs` is the RSS-specific branch. Direct callsites: `BookHelp.fetchImage`, `OkHttpStreamFetcher` (cover/manga) and `LegadoDataUrlLoader` (data-URL manga). Keep BookSource decode behavior in Runtime; AppLog diagnostics and RSS-only behavior remain host seams.
- **Glide type leak:** `AnalyzeUrl.getGlideUrl(): GlideUrl` is called only by `OkHttpStreamFetcher`; it first calls `setCookie()`, merging CookieStore cookies and setting/removing the cookie-jar marker header, then returns `GlideUrl(url, GlideHeaders(headerMap))`. The fetcher resolves source by sourceOrigin, passes source/context to AnalyzeUrl, builds OkHttp request from URL/headers, selects normal/manga client, supports failed-URL and Wi-Fi-only options, and cancels Call + SupervisorJob on cancellation/cleanup. Glide 5.0.7 + OkHttp integration/KSP are App adapter dependencies. A typed image-request value/operation must preserve cookie/header side effects; GlideUrl/GlideHeaders must not leak into Runtime.
- **Media3:** `AnalyzeUrl.getMediaItem(): MediaItem` calls `setCookie()` and ExoPlayerHelper; only direct callers found are AudioPlayService and ReviewDetailDialog playback paths. ExoPlayerHelper serializes headers into a delimiter-tagged MediaItem URI consumed by its resolving data source. Media3 1.10.1 is playback-only App dependency; keep getMediaItem/MediaItem out of Runtime.
- **AppCompat/lifecycle:** JsExtensions.showBrowser obtains the top AppCompatActivity, checks source UI suppression, dispatches to UI thread, checks finishing/destroyed/FragmentManager state and opens BottomWebViewDialog. `RssJsExtensions` owns weak Activity/source refs and `open()` uses Activity lifecycleScope on IO then Main for login/RSS/search/explore navigation and App DB access. `SourceLoginJsExtensions` extends it and inherits its method surface; it adds callback weak refs, clipboard, HttpTTS cache cleanup under lifecycleScope, toast and browser dialog. `SourceCallBack` launches lazy work in activity.lifecycleScope and executes source JS on IO. Keep these concrete bridges in App; preserve lifecycle cancellation, weak references, callback order and Main dispatch.
- **Mixed bridge caveat:** `RssJsExtensions` is not exclusively RSS UI: `ReviewController.LegacyReviewJsExtensions` subclasses it with null Activity and overrides showBrowser to a callback, while using the inherited AnalyzeRule/source-facing helper surface. `WebJsExtensions` also subclasses it and was already covered by Task 026AB. Split source-facing JS contracts from host UI behavior; do not migrate the whole RSS/login/WebView inheritance tree or silently remove inherited methods.
- **Pinned dependencies:** Glide 5.0.7; Media3 1.10.1; AppCompat 1.7.1; Lifecycle 2.10.0. Pinned App directly declares Glide + OkHttp integration + KSP, Media3 ExoPlayer + datasource-OkHttp, AppCompat, lifecycle-common-java8 and lifecycle-service (lifecycle-runtime-ktx transitive per existing Task 026K matrix). Inspected current Badcat App/Runtime/Rhino/contract Gradle files contain no direct declarations for these families. No resolved graph or variant evidence.

## 24.178 Task 026AL result — archive extraction and charset utility JS API closure

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-ARCHIVE-CHARSET-JS-UTILITY-CLOSURE-026AL; bounded read-only archive/charset API and dependency-owner closure complete. Registration start HEAD 0b12f499e013da0643733bff06999a1157f5a5b6; registration/execution HEAD fddd9a66318784cb34bf09fc7e38a749aca454b9; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a.
- **JsExtensions API:** `unzipFile`, `un7zFile`, `unrarFile` are aliases for `unArchiveFile`; it returns `ArchiveTemp/MD5-16(archive filename)` and ignores the extracted-file list. ZIP/RAR/7z string helpers expose default/explicit charset overloads; byte-array helpers return nullable bytes, fetch absolute URLs through source-bound AnalyzeUrl/context, or HexUtil-decode non-URL input. Missing entry yields null at byte level and empty string at string level; explicit invalid charset propagates.
- **Archive implementation:** ArchiveUtils accepts `.zip/.rar/.7z`, initializes a lazy `externalCache/ArchiveTemp` root via `createFolderReplace` (deletes old root), and extracts into an MD5 filename child. LibArchiveUtils uses `me.zhanghai.android.libarchive:library:1.1.6`, Android PFD/Os and Okio Buffer; native handles are freed in finally. ArchivePathUtils rejects absolute, drive-prefixed and traversal entries and checks canonical destination containment. This path traversal guard is security-critical.
- **Static source quirks / security boundary:** JsExtensions.getFile builds the path under externalCache but checks canonical containment against externalCache.parentFile; it is not strict externalCache-root confinement and may permit `../` to a sibling still under the parent. `getZipByteArrayContent` appears to call nextEntry twice after a nonmatching entry, potentially skipping alternate entries. `EncodingDetect.getEncode(File)` advances its position only for bytes `<0`, so ASCII bytes overwrite the current slot; `getTxtInFolder` can deleteCharAt(-1) on an empty but listable directory. These are source observations, not runtime tests; preserve or change only with differential evidence.
- **Charset closure:** `EncodingDetect.getEncode(bytes)` uses vendored CharsetDetector.detect() with UTF-8 fallback; file overload samples via the existing 8,000-byte algorithm. `LibArchiveUtils` independently uses `detectAll().first()` for archive entry names, with no empty-match fallback. The ICU package is eight Java files; current Badcat App copies are byte-identical to pinned upstream, but are not in Runtime. EncodingDetect is absent from current Badcat App/Runtime source tree.
- **Dependency ownership:** pinned App declares libarchive 1.1.6, DocumentFile 1.1.0, Core KTX 1.18.0 and Splitties 3.0.0; upstream packaging preserves `libarchive-jni.so` debug symbols. Badcat App directly declares libarchive 1.1.6, but Runtime/Rhino/contract do not; Runtime has no direct Okio edge although LibArchiveUtils imports Okio Buffer. If retaining LibArchiveUtils verbatim in Runtime, direct libarchive and Okio compile edges plus native ABI/packaging proof are required; otherwise use a typed ArchivePort that preserves RAR/7z and extraction behavior. Generic SAF/FileDoc/DownloadManager/local-book import/export stays App-side.
- **Evidence:** `/tmp/task026al-archive-charset/RESULT.md` SHA-256 b5221a04501976d5cd0ec7ad5b833bf668320f0eca0387b2584fa901ea3f6617; `callsite-evidence.txt` SHA-256 0c899436170fe3d5e2f8ed99e6fbe51b5acdd78b4853337492bd592fef050971; `INPUT-HASHES.sha256` SHA-256 ff9e3ed522432d7542426621ba0bc069fe61297521413c6fdd78302b97719ce1; `BADCAT-ICU-HASHES.sha256` SHA-256 7b8eaa73074e738e5ede08aff9f276fb6ae8702429cf5bcfb8dc27e2e7dd62b6; all report checksums passed.
- **Procedure:** preregistration notes limited import-matrix/method-name scoping before registration. Required lists were reread in full after registration commit before substantive source/caller inspection. No source/test/Gradle/workflow/shrinker/schema/UI/Reader files changed.
- **Boundary:** no Gradle/dependency/variant resolution, download/cache mutation, build/compiler/test/CI/DEX/R8/APK/device/network; no App compile retry under §24.119. Archive runtime parity, JNI ABI/package inclusion, path security differential, charset parity and Host Port semantics remain NOT ESTABLISHED.

## 24.182 Task 026AN result — source JS file-storage utility API and Host Port closure

- **Task:** `R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-JS-FILE-STORAGE-UTILITY-CLOSURE-026AN`; bounded read-only source/API/caller closure complete. Registration start HEAD `91c26506cc774f8f4d7e4a6d6b378a3ba511e2df`; registration commit/execution HEAD `938af6da748705bfe59db1687cb7f275fb0fc93f`; pinned upstream `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **JS API closed:** importScript; cacheFile(url)/cacheFile(url,saveTime); downloadFile(url)/deprecated downloadFile(hex,url); public Rhino getFile/readFile; readTxtFile overloads; deleteFile; getTxtInFolder. 026P method matrix rows 455, 470, 479, 518, 554, 802, 817, 826, 836, 848 and 903 are now reconciled against exact upstream helpers/callers.
- **Source helper semantics:** FileUtils.getCachePath uses appCtx.externalCache; getPath concatenates without canonical validation; createFileReplace deletes/recreates and makes parents; delete(file,true) recursively removes root via rename-then-delete. cacheFile uses MD5-16(URL), Room CacheDao metadata and a 50 MiB memory LRU; saveTime seconds, 0 means no expiry. CacheManager.putFile/getFile via ACache, source key/value, SharedJsScope shareJs ACache and physical source files are distinct stores.
- **Critical security finding:** AnalyzeUrl.UrlOption.setType accepts any nonblank string; downloadFile interpolates it into the output filename and passes it through unsanitized FileUtils.getPath. A type such as `../../../files/escape` can normalize outside externalCache and create parent directories, allowing an app-private path write. The deprecated hex overload also accepts raw type. Do not reproduce this vulnerability. A strict extension allowlist and canonical per-source-root validation are mandatory security gates, with an explicitly reviewed compatibility change.
- **Additional root issue:** JsExtensions.getFile checks canonical containment against externalCache.parentFile, not externalCache itself, and returns the original File after validation. It permits sibling paths under the parent and has a check/use symlink race. The current Badcat per-source SHA-256 root and RhinoSourceFileHandle are stricter, but the handle is not a complete java.io.File ABI.
- **Download contract:** upstream AnalyzeUrl.getInputStream uses full URL-option/request semantics, source cookies/rate limit, data URI handling and raw response stream; the callsite does not explicitly check isSuccessful. downloadFile closes input/output streams and deletes partial files on copy failure. Current Badcat strips URL options except type and calls generic httpGet with empty headers; it imposes 16 KiB URL/8 MiB body limits, checks 2xx, returns an opaque token path, and writes atomically. These are deliberate security/robustness differences, not exact parity.
- **Read/delete/folder contract:** readFile missing => null; readTxtFile missing => empty string; explicit charset invalidity propagates; auto charset uses EncodingDetect.getEncode(File), including the 026AL 8,000-byte sample-index quirk. deleteFile recursively deletes the root. getTxtInFolder iterates direct children in filesystem order without filtering directories, joins with newline, deletes folder, and can throw on an empty but listable folder. Current Badcat filters non-files/external symlinks and returns empty/cleans missing folders; no runtime differential test was run.
- **Cache and WebView split:** cacheFile uses global MD5 URL key in upstream CacheManager; current Badcat uses source-scoped SourceScriptKeyValueStore plus per-source file bytes. WebJsExtensions downloadFileAwait/readTxtFileAwait/importScriptAwait are App lifecycleScope/WebView callback adapters. Keep SourceHttpPort, SourceFilePort, SourceCachePort, SourceScriptFileCacheStore and WebView bridge ownership distinct.
- **Addendum update:** Phase B addendum §5.2 now separates SourceFilePort/FileStoragePort, ArchivePort, SourceDownload composition, SourceCachePort and SourceScriptFileCacheStore; §5.3 records JS method behavior and path traversal/security requirements. Addendum SHA-256 `ade8eb3846e9ab70f0118bd62298a9bb037400a6a795b202de9bb80ae3deace1`.

## 24.184 Task 026AO result — AnalyzeUrl.type path traversal security review

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-ANALYZEURL-TYPE-PATH-SECURITY-REVIEW-026AO; bounded read-only threat-scope review complete. Registration start HEAD `31633820118b6a8ef786f53e762a6e8c1aaa7a7d`; registration/execution HEAD `3461fa870eb865ce3e6dfffc23b7a64f07e61652`; pinned upstream `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Ingress:** AnalyzeUrl parses the comma-JSON suffix using GSONStrict then GSON and copies UrlOption.getType() directly. setType only rejects null/blank and otherwise preserves the raw string; the URL-option editor inserts unfiltered editType text into BookSource and RSS rule fields. Source JS can also supply arbitrary URL strings to @JavascriptInterface downloadFile. CurlAnalyzeUrlConverter does not accept type as a supported option.
- **Sink:** both downloadFile overloads interpolate MD5-16(url) + "." + raw type into FileUtils.getPath. FileUtils only concatenates strings; File.createFileReplace deletes an existing target or creates parent directories. The primary overload deletes its target before acquiring the network stream; the deprecated hex overload replaces/creates before hex decoding. Neither path calls JsExtensions.getFile, so its separate canonical check does not protect these writes.
- **Path proof:** for illustrative internal fallback root `/data/user/0/example.app/cache`, type `../../../files/probe.bin` normalizes to `/data/user/0/example.app/files/probe.bin`; the same pattern reaches sibling shared_prefs and databases paths. For illustrative external-cache root `/storage/emulated/0/Android/data/example.app/cache`, nine leading `../` segments followed by `data/user/0/example.app/files/probe.bin` normalize to the internal app-private files path. This is lexical normalization only; no device path was queried and no target was accessed, created, written or deleted. A single `../` is not sufficient because its first dots are concatenated to the MD5 filename; the multi-segment proof is required.
- **Root:** Context.externalCache is externalCacheDir ?: cacheDir. Exact device root is variable. No canonical containment or extension grammar exists at either pinned download sink. Encoded separators/backslash-only strings are not decoded/treated as separators by the inspected Android/Linux path builder; literal slash plus sufficient `../` segments is the demonstrated primitive.
- **Legitimate values:** no closed enum exists. The field is used as a file suffix. Confirmed book formats: txt/epub/umd/pdf/mobi/azw3/azw; archive formats: zip/rar/7z; existing Badcat fixture also uses dat. UrlUtil.getSuffix already defines a generic 1–5 ASCII-alphanumeric suffix grammar and `ext` fallback, but explicit UrlOption.type bypasses it. BookInfoViewModel has a separate 32-character display suffix grammar and is not the file-write boundary.
- **Current Badcat:** urlOptionType/downloadExtension enforce `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,5}$` and normal download falls back to validated URL suffix/`ext`; deprecated hex overload returns empty for absent/invalid type. It writes an opaque token within the source-private root. Existing source tests cover benign epub/dat, symlink/path safety and path-argument traversal but not malicious type values; tests were inspected, not executed.
- **Recommendation, not approval:** keep UrlOption.type generic for non-download consumers and validate at both downloadFile sinks. Accept only `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,5}$`; primary absent-type fallback remains UrlUtil suffix/`ext`; deprecated absent-type remains empty; invalid explicit nonblank type should fail closed before network/path mutation. Resolve a single filename beneath a canonical per-source root, reject symlinked root/target/parents, use a same-root temporary file and atomic replacement, and never delete the old target before request/write success. Decode deprecated hex before touching target. Invalid-type fallback vs rejection is a compatibility decision pending user approval.
- **Addendum:** §5.3.1 records the source ingress, sink behavior, path traversal, recommended suffix/root/atomic-write policy and decision-pending state. Addendum SHA-256 `5c04602d238a897432c806d85af4ed7d9854d055837ba719cdce076dc1806b11`.
- **Evidence:** `/tmp/task026ao-analyzeurl-type-security/RESULT.md` SHA-256 `068eb8dcd56769ea8e0d9f298abafe815e5320c27931dac685a4d9367c3673f6`; `type-ingress.tsv` SHA-256 `b6cdba9b042f8535cf4f543e1e767e3a4fbced05c2fd17f52f19076f38518179`; `path-normalization.txt` SHA-256 `bbe5d0d50c88c476b55cef5de6bf666805b194ee08def23eda00076e123b2e63`; `INPUT-HASHES.txt` SHA-256 `d594db104ef1d1bde4b39b8033999265880779e5cc469a0b826326a39b77ecb0`; all entries in `CHECKSUMS.sha256` passed. ## 24.188 Task 026AQ result — Source Cookie Store identity and lifecycle closure

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-SOURCE-COOKIE-STORE-IDENTITY-CLOSURE-026AQ; bounded read-only source/API/caller/host persistence closure complete. Registration start HEAD `cffae606d6b64a929b955a3ecb38c83bc0e353c5`; registration commit / evidence HEAD `f56e542afe561e9d1d445c60cd2524fe66ea7a12`; branch `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`; pinned upstream `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Required-list procedure:** after registration, reread `00-MASTER-WORKFLOW.md` completely (365 lines) and `03-LEGADO-RUNTIME-OVERVIEW.md` completely (1,966 lines) from the registration HEAD; reread was repeated on user's request before continuing. SHA-256: Master `02e5b09f4d135834eb4b42af50e55b32f9fbc238417954dd429c9688a9aa6468`; Overview `0fe93b01b66ce5b67cd99480f6857096ae5ab23de62dcf04991478e1e8df0516`.
- **Identity finding:** upstream cookie values are not keyed by sourceId. `CookieStore` normalizes source/request URLs through `NetworkUtils.getSubDomain`: eTLD+1, IP literal, or raw-input fallback. Room `Cookie.url` is the effective-domain key (PK + unique index); persistent and session maps are shared across all sources on that domain. `BookSource.getKey()` / Badcat DTO `sourceId` is the source URL; `getTag()` is display metadata. All source-bound BackstageWebView callers pass `source.getKey()` as its `tag`, so its cookie readback maps to the same domain bucket. Login header/info remain separately source-URL-keyed.
- **Persistence:** Room CookieDao + CacheManager memory copy for persistent values; CacheManager process memory for session values, with session overriding persistent values on merge. Session values are not in cookie backup. Optional backup encrypts all CookieDao rows; restore merges ordinary domain rows and directly inserts legacy pipe-key rows. `CookieStore.clear()` only deletes pipe-key legacy rows.
- **Source-visible API:** `cookie` is bound to CookieStore in BaseSource.evalJS, JsSourceEngine, AnalyzeUrl and AnalyzeRule. CookieStore methods include setCookie/replaceCookie/getCookie/removeCookie/cookieToMap/mapToCookie plus public setWebCookie/getKey/clear. The separate `JsExtensions.getCookie(tag[,key])` overload remains part of the Java object surface. Bound CookieStore has removeCookie(url) only; `CookieManager.removeCookie(url,key)` is an internal helper, not an upstream CookieStore overload.
- **Semantics to preserve/test:** setCookie writes nullable/empty values and catches/logs persistence errors; replaceCookie merges by name and blank input is a no-op; getCookie merges persistent+session and caps output at 4,096 characters by randomly removing names; removeCookie clears the whole effective-domain Room/cache/session bucket and WebView cookies. `cookieToMap` splits semicolon/first equals, trims ASCII whitespace, drops empty values but preserves literal `null`. `CookieStore.getKey` has a source-level raw-URL session lookup inconsistency after `getCookie` already merged normalized-domain session state. `CookieStore.setWebCookie` and `CookieManager.applyToWebView` remove all Android WebView session cookies before setting a URL's cookies. `CookieManagerExtensions.removeCookie` expires visible names for host and eTLD+1 without explicit path/domain attributes.
- **HTTP:** AnalyzeUrl uses the target request URL domain, not the sourceId, and adds the CookieJar marker when enabledCookieJar is true. OkHttp and Cronet load/save through CookieManager on marked requests/responses and redirects. Persistent/session Set-Cookie values are flattened to name/value maps; attributes are not retained. The marker must be removed before sending to origin. 026AH general HTTP transport/cancellation evidence is reused, not repeated.
- **WebView/product callers:** BackstageWebView asynchronously reads Android CookieManager after page finish and calls CookieStore.setCookie(sourceKey,cookie); Login, RSS and browser WebViews have distinct App callsites. Source editor, BaseSource logout, MCP cookie tools and backup/restore are App-owned lifecycle paths.
- **Current Badcat:** sourceId is decoded from bookSourceUrl. BadcatReadingEngineFactory passes one SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar for all sourceId clients; provider ignores sourceId and the cookie value store is domain-bucketed, directionally matching upstream sharing. Persistent JSON is in SharedPreferences and session values in a process map, not Room CookieDao/backup. Parser validation, limits, null/empty handling, expired Set-Cookie handling and header trimming differ. ## 24.190 Task 026AR result — CookieStore JS facade and WebView invalidation contract

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-COOKIE-FACADE-WEBVIEW-INVALIDATION-CONTRACT-026AR; bounded read-only API/caller/WebView invalidation review complete. Registration start HEAD ec569c071338ff5fd5b172e80ef944498196a87f; registration commit / substantive inspection HEAD dae68458278cc479c60f9d17335034227307f5ce; branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a.
- **Required-list procedure:** after registration, reread 00-MASTER-WORKFLOW.md completely (365 lines) and 03-LEGADO-RUNTIME-OVERVIEW.md completely (1,993 lines) from registration HEAD dae68458278cc479c60f9d17335034227307f5ce. Both lists were read in bounded segments through their final lines before substantive inspection.
- **026P inventory correction:** the 026P 177-row/175-unique-signature matrix covers BaseSource/JsExtensions/JsEncodeUtils declarations, not the separately bound CookieStore object. CookieStore must be inventoried as its own JS object namespace. Its source-level interface has six methods: setCookie(String,String?), replaceCookie(String,String), getCookie(String), removeCookie(String), cookieToMap(String), mapToCookie(Map<String,String>?). The @Keep concrete object adds setWebCookie(String,String), getKey(String,String) and clear(). This is nine CookieStore methods, distinct from java.getCookie(tag[,key]).
- **Badcat facade gap:** RhinoSourceCookieExtensions currently has getCookie, getKey, setCookie(non-null), replaceCookie, removeCookie(url) and removeCookie(url,key). It is missing cookieToMap, mapToCookie, setWebCookie and clear; setCookie nullability is narrower; removeCookie(url,key) belongs to CookieManager's internal helper, not CookieStore's bound object. Existing RhinoSourceScriptRuntimeTest explicitly codifies that extra overload at lines 883–946. The current getKey implementation is not the upstream implementation; upstream's second session lookup uses raw URL after normalized-domain getCookie, a source-level inconsistency already identified in §24.188.
- **clear semantics:** upstream CookieStore.clear() only calls CookieDao.deleteOkHttp() (pinned CookieStore.kt:150–152); it is not a domain/session/WebView clear. Badcat clearDomain removes the whole effective-domain persistent/session bucket and import metadata. Do not alias these operations.
- **Global WebView side effect:** upstream CookieStore.setWebCookie and CookieManager.applyToWebView both call Android CookieManager.removeSessionCookies(null) before setting pairs for one base URL (CookieStore.kt:41–53; CookieManager.kt:143–150). This is process-global session-cookie removal, not URL/domain-scoped. The source passes a null callback and does not await completion, flush or read back before continuing writes. It can remove unrelated WebView session state from other origins/features in the same process. Persistent cookies are not the target of removeSessionCookies.
- **Separate domain removal:** CookieStore.removeCookie deletes the entire effective-domain Room/cache/session bucket and invokes the imported WebView removeCookie(url) extension (CookieStore.kt:110–116). The extension expires visible names at getDomain(url) and getSubDomain(url), without explicit Path/Domain attributes (CookieManagerExtensions.kt:9–21); it is not the same operation as the global session purge.
- **BackstageWebView direction:** after page finish it reads Android CookieManager.getCookie(url) and asynchronously calls CookieStore.setCookie(tag,cookie), where source callers pass source.getKey() as tag (BackstageWebView.kt:199–205). This WebView-to-domain-store import is distinct from setWebCookie/applyToWebView store-to-WebView behavior.
- **Badcat bridge status:** DefaultProcessCookieBridge provides callback-aware URL writes, WebView readback import and bounded domain/path invalidation with callback/timeout/readback/cancellation handling. However repository-wide production search found no construction/callsite and no production invocation of syncToWebView, syncFromWebView or invalidateDomain. No SourceCookiePort declaration exists. SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar does not touch Android CookieManager; its removeCookie only clears its own domain persistent/session/import metadata. The primary factory wires store callbacks into Rhino; SourceCatalogActivity's separate runtime wires only read/remove/clear callbacks.
- **Policy brief:** exact upstream global session purge, narrower URL/domain-scoped expiry, and no implicit purge/explicit blocked behavior are documented in the result report with compatibility/security tradeoffs. CookieManager.getCookie exposes a header view, not original Domain/Path/Expires/Secure/HttpOnly attributes; a scoped alternative cannot reliably distinguish session from persistent cookies or promise complete path coverage. **No global-clear policy was selected or approved in this task.**
- **Tests inspected, not executed:** DefaultProcessCookieBridgeTest has nine Robolectric test cases for bounded observation, sync precedence, optional session-only import, scoped invalidation, callback rejection, ineffective expiry, timeout and cancellation. RhinoSourceScriptRuntimeTest codifies the non-upstream key-removal overload. No test/build/CI/Gradle/dependency resolution/DEX/R8/APK/device/network action occurred.

## 24.192 Task 026AS result — Hidden WebView SSL, mixed-content and pooled trust-boundary review

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-WEBVIEW-SSL-MIXED-CONTENT-SECURITY-REVIEW-026AS; bounded read-only source/caller/security review complete. Registration start HEAD `4225694d321fc181829e866feb2dfb32924831f9`; registration commit / substantive inspection HEAD `bb90bf905ed6adcaa6d2a902dfb6def76ff6b007`; branch `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`; pinned upstream `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Required-list procedure:** after registration, reread `00-MASTER-WORKFLOW.md` completely (365 lines) and `03-LEGADO-RUNTIME-OVERVIEW.md` completely (2,016 lines) from registration HEAD `bb90bf905ed6adcaa6d2a902dfb6def76ff6b007`, in bounded segments through their final lines, before substantive source inspection.
- **Pooled defaults:** pinned `WebViewPool` is process-global. `preInitWebView` enables JavaScript, DOM storage, `MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW`, media playback without a user gesture and `allowContentAccess=true`; `allowFileAccess` is not explicitly set. It does not set a per-source trust profile. `acquire` reuses idle views; visible acquisition can reuse any idle view, while background acquisition only selects a never-attached view. `PooledWebView` changes the `MutableContextWrapper` base context on acquisition.
- **Shared callers:** one pool serves WebViewActivity (browser), ReadRssActivity (RSS), BookInfoActivity, VideoPlayerActivity, WebViewLoginFragment, BottomWebViewDialog and BackstageWebView hidden source execution. Exact acquire/release locations are in `/tmp/task026as-webview-security/pool-caller-matrix.tsv`.
- **Release/reset gap:** `WebViewPool.release` stops loading, removes known JS interfaces/listeners and selected UI state, rebinds appCtx, then recycles through a generation-specific blank page. On finish it toggles JavaScript and resets image blocking, cache mode, viewport flags and text zoom. It does not explicitly reset mixedContentMode, allowContentAccess, allowFileAccess, DOM storage enablement/content, media autoplay, cookies, WebView cache, history or origin storage. The same WebView object is subsequently eligible for reuse by other pooled callers. This is a static cross-feature state-retention risk; actual residue was not dynamically tested.
- **SSL handling:** both BackstageWebView clients call `SslErrorHandler.proceed()` for any SSL error while the view is still owned by the active navigation context; stale/non-owned callbacks are cancelled (BackstageWebView.kt:232–254, 390–410). Four visible surfaces unconditionally proceed regardless of the SslError: WebViewActivity.kt:570–577; ReadRssActivity.kt:913–918; WebViewLoginFragment.kt:141–148; BottomWebViewDialog.kt:1232–1237. No error-class check or user confirmation is present. This accepts invalid server identity (e.g. expired/self-signed/hostname mismatch) and permits active interception of page content, cookies and login data. Backstage rule HTML can expose JavaScript interfaces, increasing the impact if an attacker can modify page content; this is a source-backed threat path, not a demonstrated exploit.
- **Mixed content/content access:** `MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW` lets HTTPS pages load HTTP subresources; `allowContentAccess=true` is global to pooled views. `allowFileAccess` is not explicitly set in WebViewPool and its effective value must be verified at runtime for supported API/target combinations; this audit does not infer it. CodeEditActivity separately disables file/content access (CodeEditActivity.kt:213–216), proving a stricter per-feature profile exists upstream.
- **Manifest transport distinction:** pinned upstream targetSdk 36 and network security config base-config permits cleartext; debug-overrides trust user and system certificates (manifest line 36; network_security_config.xml:1–13). Current Badcat targetSdk 36 and explicitly sets `usesCleartextTraffic=true` but has no networkSecurityConfig reference. Cleartext permission is separate from WebViewClient SSL-error proceed and does not itself prove invalid TLS acceptance.
- **Current Badcat:** source search found no BackstageWebView, WebViewPool, SSL callback or mixedContentMode implementation. SourceBookActivity's chapter renderer disables JS/DOM storage and explicitly disables file/content access (SourceBookActivity.kt:624–635); ReaderCssActivity previews also disable JS/file/content access (ReaderCssActivity.kt:476–480, 548–552). These isolated reader/preview WebViews are not an implementation of the pinned hidden source WebView or visible browser/login/RSS product flows. Cookie bridge code touches Android CookieManager without creating WebViews.
- **Policy alternatives:** (A) reproduce upstream unconditional SSL proceed + always-allow mixed content + shared pool: best legacy compatibility, highest MITM/downgrade/state-contamination risk; (B) strict certificate validation, block mixed content and disable file/content access unless required, isolate/clear state: safer but may break legacy sources and login pages; (C) split pools/profiles by trust boundary, retain strict TLS baseline, allow mixed content only as an explicit narrow source capability, and isolate/clear origin state on release: better isolation with greater implementation/test cost. The result report details consequences and test requirements. **No policy was selected or approved in this task.**
- **Security recommendation, not approval:** do not preserve unconditional certificate-error proceed as a default. Prefer strict certificate validation; assess legacy mixed-content exceptions separately and per-source. Task 026AR's global WebView session-cookie clearing remains a separate undecided policy. The already selected SharedJsScope trust-all/HTTPS-downgrade behavior remains confined to its dedicated URL-only shared-library client and does not authorize permissive WebView TLS.
- **Evidence:** `/tmp/task026as-webview-security/RESULT.md` SHA-256 `6d93f49e373d1d8b1597774671769f079e31a3c5f8ad954e60cd658e283f1bb6`; `INPUT-HASHES.sha256` SHA-256 `d5c098eb12d05e449c0819fd18ffb74e9e11e24bac7695025f40b66e841b21d5` (18 source/build/manifest files); `webview-security-matrix.tsv` SHA-256 `d875180c63eb0fd67062eafcb0874371127690b65f6c964b32cf125326172217`; `pool-caller-matrix.tsv` SHA-256 `df397118e64e3fe014f8eb3094d6503b1da474684bea29e8c142ff00b21c1ee3`; all `CHECKSUMS.sha256` entries passed.

No production/source/test/Gradle/shrinker/manifest/schema/UI/Reader/workflow change. `git diff --check` passed.

## 24.193 User decision — Task 026AS WebView security policy Option A approved

- **Decision:** the user selected **Option A — reproduce the pinned upstream permissive WebView behavior** from Task 026AS §24.192.
- **Approved compatibility target:** retain unconditional `SslErrorHandler.proceed()` behavior on the pinned hidden BackstageWebView and visible browser/RSS/login/BottomWebViewDialog surfaces; retain the pooled WebView defaults `MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW`, JavaScript enabled, DOM storage enabled, and `allowContentAccess=true`; retain the existing shared WebViewPool reuse model and its upstream release/reset behavior.

Do not add `allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs`, third-party cookies, new cleartext exceptions, extra JavaScript interfaces, or broader permissions under this decision. Preserve exact pinned behavior, not a generalized “disable all WebView security” interpretation.
- **Scope:** this is an explicit compatibility/security tradeoff approval for reproducing the pinned upstream WebView policy when that WebView surface is integrated. It is not an instruction to weaken ordinary source HTTP clients, Android app-wide TLS, the SharedJsScope client beyond its already separately approved policy, or Badcat's existing isolated Reader/CSS preview WebViews.
- **Risk acknowledgement:** the user-selected option retains the risks recorded in §24.192: invalid TLS server identity may be accepted; HTTPS pages may load attacker-modifiable HTTP subresources; pooled WebView state may persist across product/source trust contexts because release does not explicitly clear all origin state. This choice prioritizes source/site compatibility over these protections.
- **Implementation gate:** approval does not itself implement anything or close Phase A. Any production integration/change still requires its own preregistered task, exact pinned-source parity review, regression tests, and an explicit implementation plan. No production source, manifest, Gradle, test, workflow, UI or Reader files were changed by recording this decision.

## 24.195 Task 026AT result — AnalyzeUrl request-option and SourceHttpPort caller closure

- **Task:** `R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-ANALYZEURL-REQUEST-OPTION-HOST-PORT-CLOSURE-026AT`; bounded read-only source/API/caller closure complete. Registration start HEAD `fe7d895fb480bce2d6d3c45a369cbf89653af3ed`; registration/execution HEAD `3c66ecef706f7241f6ad54a839deba6faf94d769`; branch `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`; pinned upstream `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Required-list procedure:** after registration, fully reread `00-MASTER-WORKFLOW.md` (365 lines) and `03-LEGADO-RUNTIME-OVERVIEW.md` (2,051 lines) from registration HEAD `3c66ecef706f7241f6ad54a839deba6faf94d769`, in bounded segments through their final lines, before substantive source/caller inspection.
- **Pinned option surface:** `AnalyzeUrl.UrlOption` has 16 fields: `method`, `charset`, `headers`, `body`, `origin`, `retry`, `type`, `webView`, `webJs`, `timeout`, `followRedirects`, `dnsIp` (`resolveIp` alias), `js`, `bodyJs`, `serverID`, `webViewDelayTime`. `AnalyzeUrl` expands URL `@js`, `{{...}}` and page tokens before parsing the comma-JSON suffix; strict Gson parsing is attempted first, then legacy permissive Gson. Source headers are loaded before URL-option headers; source `proxy` is extracted into client proxy configuration and removed from the outgoing map; URL-option headers overlay afterward.
- **Method/body:** pinned AnalyzeUrl maps only POST and HEAD specially; every other method string maps to GET. HTTP `getStrResponseAwait()` sends HEAD, but `getResponseAwait()` treats HEAD as GET; WebView string-response mode treats non-POST as WebView GET. POST body is form-encoded unless JSON/XML or explicit Content-Type; non-POST request builders ignore option body. Current resolver accepts and executes PUT/PATCH/PROPPATCH/REPORT, and the transport rejects non-empty GET/HEAD body instead of ignoring it.
- **Charset:** upstream `charset` controls query/form encoding; `escape` selects legacy UTF-16-code-unit escaping. `OkHttpUtils.newCallStrResponse()` calls `ResponseBody.text()` without passing UrlOption.charset, so that option is not a response-decoding override. Current resolver rejects `escape` but passes named charset to `SourceHttpRequest.responseCharset`, which changes response decoding.
- **Headers/proxy:** upstream source header construction includes same-site-gated login headers by default; `proxy` is a special source-header key used to select `getProxyClient(proxy)` and is removed from outgoing headers. URL-option headers overlay after source header extraction. Badcat currently merges source/request headers case-insensitively, but has no proxy request field/extraction and no equivalent same-site login-header decision; source `proxy` can be emitted as an ordinary origin header. Cookie identity/storage remains separately classified in 026AQ/026AR.
- **Retry/timeout/redirect/DNS:** upstream retry defaults to zero; negative values are clamped to zero; `newCallResponse` retries all non-success, non-3xx HTTP responses for any method and does not retry IOExceptions in that loop. Badcat limits retry to 0..5 and retries selected transient statuses/IO failures only for GET/HEAD. Upstream timeout accepts positive integral number/string values through Int.MAX, sets read timeout and derives a call timeout (at least 60s or 2x read unless constructor call timeout supplied); Badcat applies one timeout equally to connect/read/write/call and rejects some integral floating JSON forms. Upstream followRedirects parser accepts bool/0/1 and sets both ordinary and SSL redirect flags; Badcat always refuses HTTPS downgrade. Upstream `dnsIp`/`resolveIp` accepts validated IPv4/IPv6 literals, applies DNS override only to the target host, and rejects proxy coexistence; Badcat rejects both option names and has no DNS field.
- **Script/WebView stages:** upstream `js` executes in the live AnalyzeUrl JS binding (`java=this`) before request; `bodyJs` transforms only the HTTP StrResponse body, after XML prefix normalization. Badcat generic SourceHttpGateway uses a generic source evaluator and applies bodyJs to SourceHttpResponse more broadly. More importantly, production `java.ajax` paths in `BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory` and `BadcatReadingEngineFactory` use direct resolver → factory → client lambdas and bypass the gateway's `js`/`bodyJs` stages. Upstream `webView`, `webJs` and `webViewDelayTime` route through BackstageWebView; Badcat rejects active webView/webJs options and has no delay field/wiring. HiddenWebView behavior is separately classified in 026AP/026AS.
- **Product metadata:** `origin` is consumed by `BookshelfViewModel` and `AddToBookshelfDialog` for source selection when adding a book; `serverID` is consumed by `WebDav.fromPath()` to select a WebDAV server. Neither is an ordinary HTTP transport field. `type` remains covered by 026AN/026AO and also controls byte-hex StrResponse mode and upload multipart MIME.
- **Response/API shape:** upstream AnalyzeUrl exposes `StrResponse`, raw OkHttp `Response`, byte-array and InputStream methods, data-URI base64 byte decoding, multipart upload, GlideUrl and MediaItem adapters. `type != null` makes getStrResponse return hex-encoded fetched bytes. Current SourceHttpRequest only carries sourceId/URL/method/headers/String body/cookie flag/one timeout/redirect/retry/responseCharset; SourceHttpResponse is a buffered text/bytes DTO. It cannot represent raw Response identity, StrResponse metadata, a live InputStream, multipart upload, data URI or full WebView result. Glide/Media3 App ownership was already classified in 026AK.
- **Caller closure:** 60 direct `AnalyzeUrl(` call expressions across 32 pinned source files. Source-workflow candidates: WebBook search/explore/detail/TOC/content; BookChapterList; BookContent; AnalyzeRule; JsExtensions ajax/connect/download/archive/font; BookHelp image fetch; DictRule. Product/adjacent callers include browser/RSS/review/audio/video/BookInfo/ReadBook, Glide, WebDAV, local book, config, direct upload and bookshelf import. The 32-file line-backed matrix is `/tmp/task026at-analyzeurl-request-options/caller-matrix.tsv`; do not move every AnalyzeUrl caller into Runtime merely because it constructs the class. `UrlOptionDialog` exposes only a subset and only POST/GET method choices; `CurlAnalyzeUrlConverter` handles only method/headers/body/followRedirects and is an App code-editor helper, not the runtime parser.
- **Critical TLS correction:** pinned `HttpHelper.okHttpClient` configures `SSLHelper.unsafeSSLSocketFactory`/`unsafeTrustManager`, `unsafeHostnameVerifier`, `followRedirects(true)` and `followSslRedirects(true)` (HttpHelper.kt:58-70). `getProxyClient(null)` returns that global client (HttpHelper.kt:150-153), and `AnalyzeUrl.getClient()` obtains `getProxyClient(proxy)` (AnalyzeUrl.kt:638-665). This corrects the earlier implication that upstream permissive TLS was isolated to SharedJsScope. The user's already selected Badcat policy remains narrower: dedicated SharedJsScope client may be trust-all/downgrade; ordinary Badcat source HTTP remains strict. This is an explicit security/compatibility divergence from pinned upstream; do not widen ordinary SourceHttpClient under the existing decision. Any reconsideration requires a separate explicit user decision. This HTTP TLS correction is distinct from WebView Option A approved in 026AS.
