## 24.199 Task 026AV result — source-visible font parser/cache/remapping utility closure

- **Task:** R3-S0-T026-PHASE-A-FONT-UTILITY-PARSER-CACHE-CLOSURE-026AV; bounded static source/API/caller/cache/parser closure complete. Registration start HEAD bf4391cd847f6a68a4ac970a718330622c36409a; registration / substantive inspection HEAD 2a7d53ac4ada15fbdbded6c50fa9d0e5deb5c869; branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9.
- **Required-list procedure:** after registration, Master Workflow (365 lines) and Runtime Overview (2,097 lines) were reread completely from HEAD 2a7d53ac4ada15fbdbded6c50fa9d0e5deb5c869 in bounded segments through their final lines before substantive inspection.
- **API surface:** five frozen 026P declarations, all unannotated with Android @JavascriptInterface but still Rhino-visible: queryBase64TTF(String?), queryTTF(Any?, Boolean), queryTTF(Any?), replaceFont(String, QueryTTF?, QueryTTF?, Boolean), replaceFont(String, QueryTTF?, QueryTTF?). Shipped ruleHelp.md calls queryTTF for base64 and URL fonts and replaceFont(..., true) to filter missing glyphs. No direct Kotlin production caller of these methods was found; the API is intended for source scripts.
- **Parser positive:** upstream QueryTTF.java and Badcat app/src/main/java/io/legado/app/model/analyzeRule/QueryTTF.java are byte-identical, SHA-256 09be94396c2ac0ad85c8a8619cb7220f56156c8fcc0ea0f6ce3607c536961709. The @Keep parser uses only JDK ByteBuffer/ByteOrder/StandardCharsets/HashMap/LinkedList and AndroidX Keep metadata; it has no fontbox/parser-library dependency. It exposes mutable Unicode/glyph maps and mapping methods.
- **Parser limits:** it requires name/head/cmap/loca/maxp/glyf tables and implements cmap formats 0/4/6 only; no format 12, CFF/CFF2 outline or TTC collection support. It does not robustly validate the SFNT directory/table offsets and lengths before ByteBuffer reads; malformed fonts can throw bounds/null errors. QueryTTF itself has no input-size ceiling. These are static source observations, not parser execution results.
- **Upstream input/cache:** queryTTF accepts String or ByteArray; other types return null. String dispatch is HTTP(S) via AnalyzeUrl(data, source=getSource(), coroutineContext=context).getByteArray(), otherwise EncoderUtils Android Base64 decode. The KDoc mentions local files, but this implementation has no local File branch. String cache key is SHA-256 of the original UTF-8 string and is checked before network fetch/Base64 decode; ByteArray key is SHA-256 of bytes. useCache=false bypasses lookup/insertion. AppCacheManager.queryTTFMap is a process-global AndroidX LruCache capacity 4, no TTL and no font-specific invalidation. String URL keys therefore retain cached parser results across remote content changes until eviction; different base64 strings for identical bytes do not share keys. Cached QueryTTF maps are mutable and shared across sources.
- **Upstream error/deprecation:** null decoded/fetched bytes return null; empty ByteArray proceeds into QueryTTF and can throw on header reads. queryTTF catches Exception, logs through AppLog and rethrows. queryBase64TTF is @Deprecated, emits a source-attributed JsExtensions.log warning (Debug.log and AppLog.putDebug), then delegates.
- **replaceFont:** upstream iterates Unicode code points, preserves its explicit blank-codepoint set, treats error-font glyph ID 0 as missing, and filter=true removes only characters whose error-font glyph is absent. If the error glyph exists but correct font reverse mapping returns 0, upstream preserves the original character even when filter=true. Badcat's copied algorithm instead drops that character when filter=true. This is a concrete semantic mismatch; the three-argument overload correctly defaults filter=false.
- **Badcat cache/input deltas:** Badcat adds source-confined readFile(path/token) input; upstream actual String branch is URL or Base64 only. Badcat enforces an 8 MiB byte cap and a pre-decode Base64 cap; upstream queryTTF has no such cap. Badcat always fetches/decodes and hashes content before cache lookup, keys by sourceId + content hash, and stores in an access-order LRU of eight entries. Thus it is source-isolated and avoids stale same-URL cache entries, but cache hits do not avoid remote fetch/decode and its key/eviction semantics differ from upstream's global four-entry input-string/byte hash cache. No explicit source invalidation hook exists.
- **Badcat HTTP/error deltas:** current URL font fetch uses injected RhinoSourceScriptRuntime httpGet -> BadcatReadingEngineFactory sourceGet, which uses WebUrlResolver/SourceRequestFactory/SourceLoginSessionRequestClient under runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO), a 15-second timeout, redirects enabled and at least one retry. It rejects non-2xx before returning. Upstream uses AnalyzeUrl with the original BaseSource and full active CoroutineContext; getByteArrayAwait returns raw response-body bytes and does not impose a 2xx-only check. Current callback does not inherit script CoroutineContext/cancellation and only BadcatReadingEngineFactory supplies it; other RhinoSourceScriptRuntime construction roots retain the default unavailable HTTP callback. Current SourceHttpResponse falls back to UTF-8 re-encoding of body text if bodyBytes is absent; upstream reads raw bytes. The user's already selected strict ordinary-source TLS policy remains a deliberate security divergence from pinned upstream's globally permissive AnalyzeUrl client; do not widen it for fonts.
- **Badcat diagnostics/API delta:** current queryTTF does not wrap exceptions with upstream AppLog diagnostics; queryBase64TTF has no @Deprecated marker or warning log. Its same-name public methods remain App-host-owned in RhinoSafeSourceJavaExtensions, not canonical Runtime.
- **Dependency/owner:** QueryTTF itself needs JDK plus AndroidX Keep only. Upstream AppCacheManager's font LruCache uses AndroidX Collection 1.6.0 (candidate already classified in 026AH/026AM); font fetch needs SourceHttpPort; deprecation/error logs need DiagnosticsPort; optional Badcat local-file input needs the existing SourceFilePort. No production SourceFontCachePort exists. Runtime should own parser/glyph remapping and cache semantics; an App cache port is optional only if host ownership is explicitly chosen with exact key/eviction semantics.

- **API matrix:** 17 declarations across 12 names: toast, longToast, log, logType, androidId, getWebViewUA, openUrl (2), showBrowser (4), openVideoPlayer (2), refreshBookInfo, refreshBookToc and refreshContent. JavascriptInterface is present on androidId/getWebViewUA/openUrl/openVideoPlayer declarations but not the other methods. All are Rhino source-script-visible regardless of that annotation. Exact rows: /tmp/task026aw-js-notification-device-product-action/declaration-matrix.tsv.
- **Script callers:** help docs cover the full public surface; ruleHelp demonstrates log and toast in source rules and image-click callbacks; rssRuleHelp demonstrates toast in RSS help; shipped dictRules uses getWebViewUA in request headers; httpTTS default scripts use toast/log in TTS login code. No direct shipped default-data call to androidId/openUrl/openVideoPlayer/showBrowser/refresh events was found beyond help/docs. Caller matrix: /tmp/task026aw-js-notification-device-product-action/script-caller-matrix.tsv. Context.openUrl extension callsites and SourceNavigationBridge are not Rhino JsExtensions callers; SourceNavigationBridge is Android WebView bridge plumbing, not Rhino, per 026U.
- **Notifications/logging:** toast/longToast call ensureActive and prefix getTag + ": " + msg.toString(); null becomes "null". Upstream toast helper posts to UI, cancels the previous shared Toast, inflates the themed custom view and catches UI exceptions. log calls ensureActive, sends Debug.log under source getKey (or global channel without a source), calls AppLog.putDebug with source-tagged text and returns the original Any? object. Debug and AppLog are separate: Debug handles active source callback/BuildConfig.DEBUG logging; AppLog.putDebug is gated by AppConfig.recordLog, stores up to 100 entries and posts APP_LOG_UPDATED. logType delegates to log("null") or the object's JVM class name and returns Unit.
- **Device identity/UA:** AppConst.androidId lazily reads Settings.System.getString(appCtx.contentResolver, Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID) and returns literal "null" on null. getWebViewUA calls WebSettings.getDefaultUserAgent(appCtx) and is used by shipped dictionary rules. Both are AppContext Host capabilities, not Runtime computation.
- **Navigation:** openUrl(url) delegates to openUrl(url,null); two-arg path rejects length >=64 KiB, checks source navigation policy, routes legado:// and yuedu:// to OnLineImportActivity before source lookup, and otherwise requires BaseSource and launches OpenUrlConfirmActivity with URI/MIME/source key/name/type. showBrowser has four overloads, checks active context/navigation policy, silently no-ops without top AppCompatActivity or source, dispatches on UI thread, rechecks finishing/destroyed/stateSaved, then opens BottomWebViewDialog with source key/URL/HTML/preload JS/config. The selected WebView Option A security policy remains separately recorded; no re-audit or policy change here.
- **Video:** two-arg openVideoPlayer delegates using VideoPlay.defaultFloatWindow; explicit overload checks source-navigation policy then SourceHelp starts VideoPlayService as foreground service for floating playback or VideoPlayerActivity otherwise, passing URL/title/source key/source type. Media3 and player UI remain App product responsibilities.
- **Product events:** refreshBookInfo/refreshBookToc/refreshContent post Boolean true to three distinct LiveEventBus tags. BookInfoActivity observes INFO and TOC; ReadBookActivity observes TOC and CONTENT; all observers require lifecycle STARTED. Events are global/fire-and-forget, contain no source/book identity and do not represent a database/cache mutation. Preserve event distinction and lifecycle gate in Badcat product adapters.
- **Current Badcat gap:** RhinoSafeSourceJavaExtensions implements provider-backed androidId, toast/longToast, UA string and pure string-return log/logType only. Its log(value) returns value?.toString().orEmpty(), performs no Debug/AppLog side effects, maps null to empty and does not return original Any?; logType returns String rather than Unit. It has no openUrl/showBrowser/openVideoPlayer/refresh methods. Main BadcatReadingEngineFactory injects platform UA, Settings.Secure.getString(contentResolver, Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID).orEmpty() and a Handler/MainLooper Toast.makeText presenter. Upstream uses Settings.System.getString(contentResolver, Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID) ?: "null"; the Settings namespace method and null fallback differ and require differential verification. It does not preserve the upstream custom toast/cancel/error behavior or ensureActive check.
- **Runtime roots:** SourceLoginUiV2Activity and SourceCatalogActivity create independent RhinoSourceScriptRuntime instances without the androidId/toast/UA providers; defaults throw for androidId/toast and use a hardcoded Android 12/Chrome 120 UA. BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory can construct another default runtime if none is passed; the main ReadingEngineFactory passes its active runtime, but this does not close other roots.
- **Host contracts:** no RuntimeNotificationPort or AppContextPort exists. HostUiPort, ProductEventPort and VisibleBrowserPort, plus HostUiAction.ShowBrowserDialog/OpenUrl/OpenVideoPlayer and ProductRefreshEvent, exist only as integration-contract declarations; no production implementations or wiring were found. Existing HostUiAction payloads can carry SourceIdentity through SourceExecutionContext, but exact URL import routing/length rules, source navigation policy, Activity lifecycle and fire-and-forget EventBus timing still need adapters. SourceExecutionContext carries Job but not the full upstream CoroutineContext/navigation suppression element, as separately noted in 026P.

## 24.203 Task 026AX result — source-visible reading/theme config snapshot API closure

- **Status:** bounded static declaration/payload/caller/Host Port review complete. Registration start HEAD b994f556fb0cbb60885440b3d7b0b368bdb5a660; registration commit and substantive inspection HEAD de3747bee4920bbd144ab3f63b5d137ede4671c7; branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a.

- **Declarations:** five public methods in pinned JsExtensions.kt: getReadBookConfig(): String and getThemeMode(): String and getThemeConfig(): String carry @JavascriptInterface; getReadBookConfigMap(): Map<String, Any> and getThemeConfigMap(): Map<String, Any?> do not. All five remain Rhino-visible. No overloads found. Exact rows: /tmp/task026ax-js-reading-theme-config/declaration-matrix.tsv.
- **ReadBookConfig selection:** both reading methods use ReadBookConfig.durConfig, not a copied DTO. It selects comicStyleSelect when global isComic is true, otherwise readStyleSelect; getConfig is synchronized; if fewer than five configs remain it resets to DefaultData.readConfigs and asynchronously saves readConfig.json, then falls back to configList[0] for an invalid index. The getter can therefore trigger persistence/resource-generation side effects. The getter remains the selected configList entry even when shareLayout is true; it is not the config property that selects shareConfig.
- **ReadBookConfig JSON vs Map:** getReadBookConfig Gson-serializes the 82-property Config object; Gson default null omission applies and @Transient derived color caches are excluded. Six nullable tip*Template properties serialize only when non-null. getReadBookConfigMap returns a fresh 82-key toMap projection that omits those six template properties but includes six private transient textColorInt* / textAccentColorInt* values, potentially still -1 before color initialization. It also passes through the reviewIconSvgTemplates List reference without deep copy. Kotlin declares read-only Map; actual Rhino/Java mutation behavior was not dynamically tested. The JSON and Map payloads are therefore observably different contracts.
- **Theme mode:** AppConfig.themeMode initializes from PreferKey.themeMode with "0" fallback and is refreshed by the SharedPreferences listener; the listener also updates isEInkMode and increments ResourceThemeGeneration. "1" means light, "2" dark, "3" e-ink, other values follow system night mode for isNightTheme; getThemeMode returns an unknown stored string unchanged. The Elvis "0" in the JS method is redundant because the property is non-null.
- **ThemeConfig snapshot:** each call to ThemeConfig.getDurConfig(appCtx) creates a new nine-property Config from the current theme mode, day/night name and preference values, with Android resource color fallbacks. Day defaults are md_brown_500 / md_red_600 / md_grey_100 / md_grey_200; night defaults are md_blue_grey_600 / md_deep_orange_800 / md_grey_900 / md_grey_850. Transparent navigation defaults false, background blur 0, and backgroundImgPath may be null. E-ink mode maps to non-night and therefore the day branch. Theme Map includes all nine keys including null backgroundImgPath; Gson JSON omits that null key. The map contains scalar values only and is freshly built. getDurConfig reads active preferences/resources, not a selected saved preset in ThemeConfig.configList.
- **Gson behavior:** GSON inherits default Gson null omission, uses pretty printing and disables HTML escaping; it does not call serializeNulls. The two JSON methods serialize Config values, not the Map projections.
- **Callers:** exact-name repository search found declarations, jsHelp.md documentation and code-completion entries only. No shipped default-data/source script invocation or matching current Badcat production implementation was found. Help docs define theme modes 0/1/2/3.
- **Badcat gap:** RhinoSafeSourceJavaExtensions has none of the five methods. RuntimeHostPort.kt declares neither RuntimeConfigPort nor ResourcePort; there is no production config/resource adapter or injection. Main BadcatReadingEngineFactory wires UA/Android ID/toast but not config snapshots. SourceCatalogActivity and SourceLoginUiV2Activity create separate runtimes with narrower callback sets. BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory, LegadoSourceLoginUiV2Service and RhinoEmbeddedUrlScriptEvaluator also allow independent default runtime construction. Default runtime UA remains hardcoded Android 12/Chrome 120; Android ID and toast defaults throw.
- **Owner disposition:** Runtime should own JS method names, return types and snapshot orchestration. App must own actual ReadBookConfig selection/state/durable files/transient caches, AppConfig theme preference/listener state, ThemeConfig preference/resource resolution and Android generated-R color defaults. A typed RuntimeConfigPort should expose the five distinct snapshot operations; the App implementation resolves Android resource colors internally. A separate Runtime-facing ResourcePort is not required for these five methods alone. Do not migrate Reader/theme UI or the full AppConfig/ThemeConfig subsystem into Runtime. These port names remain proposed/classified, not implemented or signature-frozen.

No Kotlin default parameter exists on the 3-argument boolean overload.
- **Entry behavior:** all three require the active Rhino context and a non-null source through SourceVerificationHelp; helper rejects main-thread calls and URLs of length 64 KiB or greater. startBrowser and startBrowserAwait apply AppConfig.blockSourceNavigation plus the operation-scoped SuppressSourceNavigation context element: blocked startBrowser silently returns; blocked startBrowserAwait throws NoStackTraceException. getVerificationCode does not consult this navigation suppression gate.
- **Coordinator/serialization:** SourceVerificationHelp owns a process-global ReentrantLock serializing all interactive verification prompts, per-attempt UUIDs, waiter Thread references, AtomicReference one-shot results, CountDownLatch/LockSupport waits, a concurrent flight registry and a close-UI callback. UI attach/cancel is synchronized against attempt removal. Cancellation/interruption removes the UUID and invokes the close callback; Activity finish is posted to main and the waiter waits at most five seconds for finish. Empty result is the cancellation sentinel and is rejected as a verification result.
- **Browser single-flight:** joining is enabled only for browser=true, refetchAfterSuccess=true and html=null. Flight key is sourceType + sourceKey + URL scheme + host + port after stripping AnalyzeUrl option suffix; path/query are not part of the key. One owner launches the browser UI. Same-source/type/origin followers wait up to five minutes and then refetch their own original URL; owner abandonment allows a follower to retry/elect a replacement; owner errors propagate. The owner wait itself has no absolute timeout and polls cancellation/interruption every second. Image-code, supplied-html and capture-only calls do not join a flight.
- **Browser result modes:** WebViewModel initializes the source by key/type, creates AnalyzeUrl with source/context, resolves base URL and headers, and uses the initial HTTP body as html for POST. On verification success, refetchAfterSuccess=true reuses supplied initial html, otherwise refetches the original URL with AnalyzeUrl and the source context; refetchAfterSuccess=false captures document.documentElement.outerHTML and current WebView URL. A coalesced follower performs its own AnalyzeUrl refetch. The returned StrResponse falls back to the original URL when the captured URL is empty.
- **Image-code flow:** getVerificationCode launches VerificationCodeActivity/VerificationCodeDialog with image URL, source key/name/type and UUID; OK stores the entered code and dismisses. Cancel/destroy writes an empty sentinel, which surfaces as NoStackTraceException("验证结果为空"). No owner timeout exists. The dialog loads the image with source-origin context and supports PhotoDialog.

## 24.207 Task 026AZ result — direct JsExtensions HTTP API and caller closure

- **Status:** complete for the bounded read-only source/API/caller/Host Port closure only. Registration start HEAD c8f9c1131e58540f18a9b7fe794c107c65cf95c6; registration and substantive inspection HEAD ed31e0b4c08d5990a652c8ce287857aa1d1978a6; branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a.
- **Declarations:** 15 unannotated Rhino-visible pinned declarations: ajax (2), ajaxAll (2), ajaxTestAll (2), connect (3), get (2), head (2), post (2). ajax/connect use AnalyzeUrl; get/head/post use Jsoup directly. These are distinct public HTTP surfaces, not one generic request wrapper.
- **Signature/docs mismatch:** pinned ajax(url, callTimeout) and connect(url, header, callTimeout) use Long?; jsHelp documents Int?. get/head/post use Int? milliseconds and default to 30,000ms. ajaxTestAll timeout is Int milliseconds. Current Badcat ajax has no callTimeout overload; connect widens header to Any?; current one-argument get(urlOrKey) is an extra heuristic method, not an upstream JsExtensions HTTP overload.
- **ajax:** upstream takes Any, uses the first element if the argument is a Kotlin List, constructs AnalyzeUrl with the current source and active Rhino CoroutineContext, returns StrResponse.body, logs AppLog on failure and returns stackTraceStr; ensureActive rethrows cancellation. Current Badcat sourceAjax partially resolves Legado URL options but does not execute js/bodyJs stages, defaults to 15s (capped at 30s), caps retry at 3 and body at 8 MiB, rejects non-2xx, has no callTimeout overload or AppLog, and catches cancellation as a returned stack trace string.
- **ajaxAll/ajaxTestAll:** upstream creates one AnalyzeUrl per URL and uses runBlocking(active context), mapAsync(AppConfig.threadCount), flowOn(IO); mapAsync awaits deferreds in input order, preserving result order while requests execute concurrently. AppConfig.threadCount defaults to 32. skipRateLimit is forwarded to AnalyzeUrl. ajaxTestAll passes callTimeout=timeout and isTest=true; success callTime is elapsed milliseconds and transport errors map to -1..-7. Current Badcat uses a fixed executor capped at 4, ordered invokeAll, sourceGet/GET callbacks and no per-URL AnalyzeUrl/UrlOption parse. Its previously audited input limits (20 URLs, 64 KiB total, 16 KiB each) are reused from §24.41.
- **ajaxTestAll production error gap:** the Rhino bridge traverses nested causes up to 16 levels and maps the upstream negative callTime codes, but BadcatReadingEngineFactory converts EngineResult.Failure into IllegalStateException(message) without preserving the cause. Consequently real production transport failures can lose SocketTimeout/UnknownHost/Connect/Socket/SSL identity and collapse to -7; tests that inject the original exception directly do not prove the production adapter path.
- **connect:** upstream parses optional header JSON with getOrNull (malformed JSON silently yields no header override), builds AnalyzeUrl with source, active context and optional callTimeout, so URL-option method/body/headers/timeout/retry/redirect semantics apply. It logs failures and returns synthetic StrResponse(url, stackTraceStr). Current Badcat always dispatches GET; explicit timeout only changes transport timeout, not method/body. It does not parse URL-option method/body. Its header parser is stricter and throws on malformed JSON. The shipped bookSources.json login example uses connect with URL-option POST/body, so this is a concrete compatibility gap.
- **get/head/post:** upstream uses Jsoup.connect with explicit headers only, adds CookieJar marker when source.enabledCookieJar, applies source ConcurrentRateLimiter blocking, installs SSLHelper.unsafeSSLSocketFactory, timeout default 30,000ms, ignoreContentType=true, followRedirects=false and executes GET/HEAD/POST. post uses requestBody(body). These callsites do not merge the source's static header map or login headers; the marker is present in source code but its actual interception by the Jsoup transport is not established in this static audit. Jsoup HTTP-error exception behavior is left at its default.
- **Current get/head/post:** Badcat resolves relative paths against source.baseUrl, merges source static headers and explicit headers case-insensitively, and uses the source cookie/login-session client. It defaults to 30s/no redirects, but adds at least one retry for GET/HEAD. SourceRequestClient returns non-2xx responses as values, whereas upstream Jsoup normally throws for HTTP error statuses. POST body content type is inferred by the Badcat request encoder; upstream directly calls requestBody(body). The return type is a custom RhinoSourceHttpResponse, not org.jsoup.Connection.Response, so method identity and response surface differ.
- **One-argument get:** current Badcat combines URL fetch and source key-value lookup using a URL-like string heuristic. Upstream BaseSource.get(key) and JsExtensions.get(url,headers[,timeout]) are separate API owners. Do not treat this convenience method as an upstream JsExtensions overload.
- **Headers/cookies:** upstream ajax/connect/ajaxAll/ajaxTestAll use AnalyzeUrl source header/login-header/cookie behavior. The Jsoup get/head/post path parses explicit Map/JSON headers and adds only the cookie marker. Badcat SourceRequestFactory merges static source headers and per-request headers, and SourceLoginSessionRequestClient can add same-site login headers. The transport contract is SourceRequestClient with SourceHttpRequest/SourceHttpResponse; there is no interface named SourceHttpPort.
- **Rate/concurrency:** upstream ajax family uses suspend AnalyzeUrl limiter calls and active coroutine context; direct Jsoup methods use ConcurrentRateLimiter.withLimitBlocking. Current bridge uses LegadoConcurrentRateLimiter Thread.sleep for all methods and callback requests runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO). The broader context/dispatcher boundary is already covered by 026AI; this task records only the direct HTTP effects.
- **TLS security boundary:** upstream ajax/connect/ajaxAll/ajaxTestAll inherit the global unsafe AnalyzeUrl OkHttp client identified in 026AT. Upstream get/head/post explicitly install SSLHelper.unsafeSSLSocketFactory, whose TrustManager accepts any certificate chain; these three Jsoup callsites do not explicitly set unsafeHostnameVerifier. Badcat ordinary SourceRequestClient remains strict TLS and blocks HTTPS downgrade per the user's explicit security choice. This is a deliberate compatibility delta; do not weaken ordinary source HTTP or change the SharedJsScope-only trust-all decision.
- **Callers:** js_source_template.js uses ajax for search/explore/detail/TOC/content; coverRule.json uses ajaxAll; httpTTS.json uses ajaxTestAll for endpoint health/latency; bookSources.json uses connect with URL-option POST/body and login headers; jsHelp/ruleHelp/rssRuleHelp document the direct helpers. No Kotlin production caller of these java helpers was found. Existing Badcat tests cover HTTP method/timeout paths, custom one-arg get, ajaxAll order/concurrency/skipRateLimit and ajaxTestAll error codes; all were inspected only. No tests were run.
- **Evidence:** /tmp/task026az-direct-http-api/RESULT.md SHA-256 5bc577eab1b47f230d308187f30c7fa52f73b6239c17a5628bb071c669894a58; declaration matrix a437d345f08a2ca42453510a9fa6e822bfae77ba67be75162bbca87ea07770e7; request/response matrix 99a7840d386c1c5038d72a4ca6fa5730517cd94ab105fd4f2a0cffeaa17da59b; caller matrix a8c6a8623a9fbe77befb11715bdc7ea96b137dfcd6efed4558e047bd03f2be88; port gap matrix e913658dd7f17cdbfbb32ceac42d3dd3d8d3bc4cd0ed5a21bf60ce539ba67448; test matrix d4bbb725eaedef65f08266dd0ed639dd7c19a4ea1a041db7de5efc90d6a71d21; input manifest 21a4575ed1eece2be87e77b7cb154fde4e2eb4213b2068f7d2e7ff7bce9b38da; CHECKSUMS.sha256 0c140c8f58188da2efc60de19528a84e36a6e85761e319df3bf57aa8e94b20af; all entries passed.

Current Cipher.doFinal returns a JS object whose only byte conversion is UTF-8 toString(), not byte[]. Current Java Base64 encoder decodes byte[] as UTF-8 then re-encodes a String, corrupting arbitrary binary. Arrays.copyOfRange rejects end > source length instead of Java's zero-padding semantics; Arrays.copyOf is absent. String.getBytes ignores charset and always UTF-8; Packages.java.lang.String and String(byte[],charset) are absent.

AES helper restricts key lengths to 16/24/32 bytes, IV to 16 bytes and mode to ENCRYPT/DECRYPT. - **ClassShutter/Badcat:** pinned Rhino ClassShutter does not deny URL, URLConnection, HttpURLConnection, HttpsURLConnection, okhttp3.HttpUrl/OkHttpClient or org.jsoup.Connection; it blocks URLClassLoader and selected file/reflection classes. It is a denylist, not a narrow allowlist. Badcat replaces Packages with a plain JS object: java.net and okhttp3 are absent; org.jsoup exposes Jsoup.parse only, with no Jsoup.connect or Connection. The custom JavaImporter implements importPackage only; no native class-argument or instance importClass behavior. Global importClass remains a distinct native Rhino helper and its compatibility with a plain JS shim object is not proven.
- **Current transport contract:** the actual interface is SourceRequestClient, not an interface literally named SourceHttpPort. SourceHttpRequest contains sourceId, URL, method, Map<String,String> headers, String body, cookie flag, one timeoutMillis, followRedirects, retryCount and responseCharset. SourceHttpResponse contains status/final URL/multi-value response headers/String body/contentType/statusMessage/callTime/optional bodyBytes. It has no request byte[]/stream, live response InputStream, errorStream, raw OkHttp/Jsoup response identity, separate connect/read timeout, proxy or multi-value request headers.
- **Current concrete transport:** SourceRequestFactory validates absolute credential-free HTTP(S), merges headers case-insensitively and prepares supported URL options. OkHttpSourceRequestClient applies 8 MiB request/response limits, header limits, source-cookie-jar injection, default 20s connect/45s read/30s write/60s call timeouts, GET/HEAD-only transient retries, cancellable async Call.cancel, followRedirects with followSslRedirects(false), and an additional redirect guard. It buffers and closes the response before returning the DTO. SourceHttpGateway performs URL-option JS/bodyJs stages around this client. RhinoSourceHttpResponse is a buffered compatibility facade, not an actual OkHttp or Jsoup Response.
- **Ownership and wiring:** no native URL/URLConnection, OkHttpClient/Call/Response or Jsoup Connection is exposed by RhinoSafeSourceJavaExtensions. The reading factory wires bounded HTTP callbacks; alternate roots have different/default callback wiring already recorded in 026AZ. No direct native Java network bridge exists. Existing cached App/contract dependencies include OkHttp 5.4.0, Jsoup 1.23.2 and Okio 3.17.0; this is artifact/API inspection only, not Runtime variant-resolution proof.
- **Transport semantics:** URLConnection is blocking; timeouts are milliseconds; POST writes bytes to output stream and caller must close/disconnect. Non-2xx getInputStream may fail while getErrorStream is separate; no error-stream corpus caller was retained. OkHttp Call.execute blocks, enqueue is asynchronous, cancel must be explicitly connected; ResponseBody is one-shot and body/response close releases resources. Jsoup Connection is a network client and also exposes proxy, cookieStore, sslSocketFactory, cookies, InputStream data, arbitrary method/body and redirects.
- **Security boundary:** ordinary source HTTP remains strict TLS and must not downgrade HTTPS to HTTP. Trust-all/SSL-downgrade remains limited to the dedicated SharedJsScope fetch client. The upstream global unsafe AnalyzeUrl client is an explicit security compatibility divergence already recorded in 026AT. WebView Option A is separate and does not authorize permissive HTTP clients. Raw URLConnection, OkHttp builder or Jsoup Connection would bypass SourceRequestClient cookie identity, rate limiting, cancellation, byte limits and TLS/redirect policy.
- **Typed adapter disposition:** future Java-style compatibility should use narrow facades over SourceRequestClient, not native network classes. Preserve only source-observed constructors/methods and semantics; enforce HTTP(S)/credential policy, strict TLS, redirects, source cookie identity, rate limiting, timeouts, request/response byte limits, cancellation and deterministic close. A parser-only HttpUrl facade may be evaluated separately, but must not leak URL.openConnection. Do not expose URLStreamHandlerFactory, global request-property/redirect setters, Socket, OkHttp builder SSL/proxy/DNS/interceptor/cookie controls, Jsoup proxy/cookieStore/sslSocketFactory, or RequestBody File/FileDescriptor/Path factories. Do not widen ClassShutter or provide unrestricted Packages traversal.
- **Unresolved:** exact URLConnection timeout literals, RequestBody factory overload, complete Request.Builder chain, source-specific non-2xx/error-stream branches and raw response stream usage are not established from the preserved corpus summaries. They require immutable source snapshot bytes or a separate evidence task.

## 24.221 Task 026BG result — batch-content and source-navigation context Host Port contract closure

- Status: complete for bounded read-only source/caller/lifecycle/identity/Host Port contract closure. Registration start HEAD e55f1458a48fdd6b786763b1544b6431bfd61025; registration commit / execution source HEAD ad1a3a98bdb4b60d65a0df1b8d6bb6a5b7b3f4a1; branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; pinned upstream 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8b7a4132c784da9a.
- Required-list procedure: after registration, Master Workflow (365 lines) and Runtime Overview (2,379 lines) were reread completely from registration/execution HEAD ad1a3a98bdb4b60d65a0df1b8d6bb6a5b7b3f4a1 through their final lines before substantive inspection.
- Upstream batch entrypoints: standard BookContent.analyzeContentBatch and JS JsSourceBook.getContentBatchAwait both create BatchContentContext with current CoroutineContext and per-index BookHelp.contentSaveToken, execute the corresponding JavaScript rule/function, close in finally and return unsaved chapters. JsSourceEngine installs its batchContext only around getContentBatch. WebBook dispatches standard vs JS. BookSource.supportContentBatch requires ruleContent/maxBatchSize>1 and, for standard sources, nonblank contentBatch; JS sources require a paired getContentBatch/maxBatchSize config. Batch size clamps to 1..50.
- cacheContent contract: public @JavascriptInterface callback takes Any? chapter identifier and String content, returns Boolean, unwraps Rhino Wrapper, requires a live batch context, then delegates to BatchContentContext.saveContent. getBatchContext defaults null and is overridden only during the active standard/JS batch. Outside batch, cacheContent throws.
- Batch identity: BookChapter object resolves by index only; CharSequence resolves through unique original/absolute/normalized URL aliases; duplicate URLs remain ambiguous; numeric identifiers are rejected. A foreign BookChapter object with the same index can resolve because the upstream implementation compares index only, not book/source identity.
- Batch save lifecycle: one synchronized lock guards active/closed state, identifier resolution, source replaceRegex, blank detection, save-token validation, BookHelp.saveContent and savedIndexes. Replacement runs with the chapter/base URL and batch CoroutineContext. Blank/stale saves return false; missing token and ambiguous/unknown identifiers throw. close prevents late writes; missingChapters preserves original order.
- Save tokens: upstream ContentSaveKey is bookUrl+chapterIndex, with folderName/version in ContentSaveToken. CacheBook.runBatch captures an outer token map before calling WebBook; BookContent/JsSourceBook independently capture an inner token map while creating BatchContentContext. They are not explicitly shared or equality-checked. The existing Android stale-edit test edits after the batch network request has started, not in the pre-context token-capture gap. This audit does not claim a reproduced overwrite; it records the two-snapshot seam and requires one shared token snapshot or a dedicated race proof in any Host Port design.
- Partial success: if a batch script fails after some chapters are saved, CacheBook preserves saved chapters and returns only missing/blank chapters to single-chapter fallback. It checks outer tokens before consuming content, then saves images and posts normal success. Cancellation releases batch tickets in finally. ReadBook prefetch and CacheBook manual download both batch only eligible pending chapters, and require at least two.
- App ownership: BatchContentContext, BookSource, Book, BookChapter, BookHelp, Room, file paths, CacheBook tickets, save events and image processing are App Host-owned. Do not move these entities or persistence into Runtime.
- Upstream navigation context: SuppressSourceNavigation is an operation-local CoroutineContext marker. Suppression is enabled only when current AppConfig.blockSourceNavigation is true AND the operation context contains the marker. The setting is checked at action time. The marker alone or preference alone does not globally block unrelated work.
- Context propagation: JsExtensions.getSourceNavigationContext defaults to EmptyCoroutineContext; JsExtensions.context combines active RhinoContext coroutineContext with getSourceNavigationContext. WebJsExtensions returns its captured navigationContext. AnalyzeRule strips ContinuationInterceptor but retains Job/custom elements; JsSourceEngine passes CoroutineContext into script eval; AnalyzeUrl strips ContinuationInterceptor and retains remaining context. BaseSource.evalJS has no explicit CoroutineContext parameter and does not pass one to RhinoScriptEngine.eval, so universal context inheritance must not be assumed.
- WebView bridge: BackstageWebView passes the suspended operation's block.context into load/createWebView, re-queries a fresh BookSource from Room, applies withSourceNavigationContext(context) and constructs WebJsExtensions with the same context. The proxy is required because WebView JavaScriptInterface callbacks execute on a different Java thread. It runs login under the captured context but gates openUrl/openVideoPlayer. Login and HTTP remain functional while incidental navigation/browser/video UI is blocked.
- Upstream suppression call sites include CheckSourceService domain check; ChangeBookSourceViewModel search/detail/change flows; ChangeChapterSourceViewModel content/cache flows; and WebBook search. Only the marker-bearing operation is affected; parallel reader/login operations remain interactive. SourceNavigationPolicyTest and SourceNavigationUiTest cover the marker+opt-in and UI/HTTP/login behavior.
- Current Badcat batch gap: ReadingEngine has no batch operation; SourceChapterContentService loads one chapter at a time; CssChapterContentParser rejects contentBatch; BookSource stores raw ruleContentJson/rawJson but no typed contentBatch/maxBatchSize; codec checks maxBatchSize numeric exact integer but does not apply upstream >1/maximum-50 eligibility or JS function-pair semantics. No getContentBatch engine exists.
- Current Badcat cache: ChapterContentCache/FileChapterContentCache provide single-chapter sourceId+bookUrl+chapterIndex keys, process-wide generation fencing, AtomicFile, 4 MiB entry and 64 MiB total limits. SourceChapterContentService uses a 12-hour TTL and 20-page cap. It has no batch session, per-batch save map, URL alias resolver, missing-chapter fallback or close lifecycle. Upstream token key omits sourceId and includes folderName/version; Badcat adds sourceId. Do not silently remove that product identity difference.
- Current bridge/context gap: RhinoSafeSourceJavaExtensions.getBatchContext returns null, cacheContent always throws, and getSourceNavigationContext always returns EmptyCoroutineContext. SourceExecutionContext contains SourceIdentity/caller/operationId/navigationPolicy/Job but no full CoroutineContext, suppression marker or book/chapter/batch identity. Repository search found only the contract test constructor and declaration, no production constructor. SourceNavigationPolicy ALLOW/BLOCK is only referenced by the contract test. HostUiAction/HostUiPort are declarations with no production implementation/caller; no BatchContentPort or SourceNavigationContextPort exists.
- Potential Rhino visibility: upstream getBatchContext is public but not @JavascriptInterface. Android WebView therefore does not expose it; Rhino public-member wrapping may expose it, including BatchContentContext public bookSource/book/chapters and save/resolve/close/status methods. No external corpus call to getBatchContext itself is recorded. A safe future facade should not leak those App entities or mutation internals by default.
- Candidate Host Port contract: BatchContentPort opens a one-use BatchContentSession from source/book identity, ordered chapter references and execution context; Host owns tokens, URL aliases, replacement, persistence, events and images. Session exposes only cacheContent(identifier,content): Boolean, ordered missing indexes and close. The callback is synchronous while Badcat ChapterContentCache.put is suspend; implementation must explicitly bridge this (bounded worker-thread synchronous adapter with cancellation, or a suspend-capable script model), never block UI or swallow cancellation. Share one save-token snapshot across scheduler/session or prove the capture gap safe.
- Candidate navigation contract: SourceNavigationContextPort carries operation-local marker plus source/operation identity and parent Job. HostUiPort checks marker AND current user preference at dispatch for OpenUrl/OpenVideoPlayer/ShowBrowserDialog and returns Blocked(SOURCE_POLICY). Preserve login/HTTP allowance and WebView fresh-DAO binding. Context must be immutable and contain no Activity/View.
- Evidence: RESULT.md SHA-256 64e3bcc3ab550419261d21ded5b141fe1bfd5f2f29a103993e12f68f52327e0c; batch method/caller matrix 30cb3563f7997fac12d12e16e193bc473134057dc1d8e6f2af1e2e96f4945f46; batch lifecycle/identity matrix 3a3f3d9e4bc09fce4d07586416ca9831c50b2328b6e837654d41da108b610fc9; navigation context flow matrix 06d803982ffbcd8b138a707b0e14e443323ac8bab2f0babd1c6c345f61a4359a; Badcat Host Port gap matrix 94443738371c37a43a2d42cc8901fc9bd9a3c3f4a86efc160cfc9a41a86f002a; Host Port contract 93eaea4d0b5cdf2727ac59a364f4b04ad932a450f00e0f0a4a6eb3512b7d24fe; policy test matrix 2e4311b66ceeb940f638d46ba164b9f3dccd4244adafc3f1ecab187a044e5996; input manifest a27f1cebf8aebb404d11327426d54e5cb8a84a2d68cfbbb55400fcfaf2f2831f; CHECKSUMS 0770af5e0f166c32aa82697fc4e69626e6ea3e3890f40342657613414a0e2d91; all checksums passed.
- Validation boundary: no Gradle/dependency/variant resolution, download/cache mutation, build/compiler/test/CI/DEX/R8/APK/device/network/source-rule execution; no App compile retry under §24.119; no production/source/test/Gradle/shrinker/schema/database/UI/Reader/workflow changes.

## 24.236 Task 026BO scope amendment — preserve Git blob identity without inventing SPDX file checksums

- **Trigger:** 026BN's immutable evidence contains each selected C source's GitHub Git blob SHA-1 and SHA-256 of the first-100-line header excerpt, but does not retain complete source-file bytes. A Git blob object ID is not the raw-file SHA-1 checksum because Git hashes the object header and content; the header-excerpt SHA-256 is not a checksum of the complete source file. Neither may be placed in an SPDX File checksum field as if it hashed the complete file.
- **Amended file-level deliverable:** create a separate checksum-verified FILE-LICENSE-EVIDENCE.tsv sidecar with one row for each of the 123 selected C translation units and eight relevant headers. Preserve exact source path, immutable Git blob SHA-1 (explicitly labeled Git object ID), header-excerpt byte count/SHA-256 (explicitly labeled excerpt), license classification, SPDX expression or NOASSERTION, exact exception note, source commit and recursive tree. Do not fabricate SPDX File objects or raw-file checksums.
- **SPDX package representation:** add source-only package nodes for the exact libarchive/codec revisions, with libarchive aggregate package license left NOASSERTION because of file-level exceptions. Keep filesAnalyzed false where full source bytes are unavailable. Add exact license declarations only for component scopes supported by 026BM; use extracted LicenseRef text for custom bzip2/UC Regents/public-domain notices where exact text is present. Do not create a binary/source relationship.
- **Binary representation:** preserve the four AAR ELF payloads as separate binary package/file evidence with observed AAR member path, size, SHA-256 and Build ID; their license and source relationship remain NOASSERTION. The AAR wrapper package remains separate from its embedded native payload.
- **Validation amendment:** validate the SPDX package/relationship/custom-license structure and the sidecar's one-to-one coverage against the 123+8 source matrix rows. Explicitly report that no raw source-file SHA-256 or SPDX File checksum is available for the source-only rows. All other 026BO scope and exclusions remain unchanged.
- **Status:** this amendment narrows the deliverable to preserve SPDX correctness; it does not reduce the required source/license coverage. ### 24.265.2 Task 026CT result — BatchContent and AnalyzeUrl source closure audited (2026-11-28)

- **Identity:** registration HEAD 3df7aa8cc05c934110d35ea074d7581da2c3befb; fixed Legado 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a. Report /tmp/task026ct-batch-model-closure/RESULT.md, SHA-256 8c43b9644b11ebac857d9520e06b3a29b73172cf5e125c146f47454a4df81edd.
- **Exact upstream types:** Book (33 fields), BookChapter (17 fields), BookSource, BaseSource, BaseBook, RuleDataInterface, AnalyzeUrl (1,052-line request/JS object), BatchContentContext, ContentSaveToken (declared in BookHelp.kt) and BookHelp. None of the six requested exact FQCNs exists in Badcat production modules; the host BookChapter DTO is a separate seven-field type.
- **Identity:** Book is keyed/equal by bookUrl. BookChapter Room primary key is (url,bookUrl), unique index is (bookUrl,index), and its equals/hashCode compare url only. BatchContentContext deliberately uses chapter.index as identity, supports raw/absolute/normalized URL aliases, and rejects ambiguous URL-only identifiers. Save fence key is (bookUrl,chapterIndex), not URL.
- **Batch lifecycle:** ordinary contentBatch and JS getContentBatch callers capture current CoroutineContext and one BookHelp.ContentSaveToken per chapter, invoke rule/JS with live Book/BookChapter objects, close context in finally, and return unsaved chapters for single-chapter fallback. cacheContent unwraps Rhino Wrapper and requires active batch context.
- **Token/save semantics:** ContentSaveToken has internal constructor/key/folder; BookHelp owns the private in-memory ContentSaveFence. saveContent validates bookUrl/index/folder and only publishes if captured version is current; optional metadata update writes Room DAO; success posts SAVE_CONTENT event. The file, optional DAO update and event are not one cross-store transaction.
- **AnalyzeUrl closure:** the initial lexical inventory contained 32 AnalyzeUrl references; 026DJ later refines this to 29 constructor-caller files / 57 callsites (plus one declaration, one type-only reference and one false positive). It is a 1,052-line executable URL-option/JS/HTTP object, not a DTO. It binds java/baseUrl/cookie/cache/page/key/speech/book/source/result/infoMap/extraParams and shared CoroutineContext; supports request options, cookies, rate limit, HTTP, proxy/Cronet/DNS, WebView, upload and multiple response types (StrResponse, okhttp Response, bytes, InputStream, GlideUrl, MediaItem).
- **Current host delta:** app.badcat.engine.BookChapter is a seven-field DTO and does not have the pinned entity FQCN/methods. SourceRequestFactory/SourceHttpGateway implement a bounded URL/HTTP subset, not live Book/BookChapter/BaseSource bindings, complete UrlOption, cookie/shared scope/WebView/upload/response lifecycle. ChapterContentCache uses a separate host token/fence and stores parsed/purified ChapterContent JSON, not BookHelp raw content.
- **Source closure blocker:** copying Book/BookChapter/BookSource/BaseSource/AnalyzeUrl/BatchContentContext/BookHelp as-is into :legado-runtime would import Room, appDb, AppConfig, Reader, WebView, CookieStore, Android UI, SAF/files, EventBus, Glide/Media3, HTTP and other App-only dependencies, violating the selected Runtime→App/DAO boundary. The minimum authentic model/service split must be designed before implementation; no DTO substitute is acceptable.
- **Decision:** BatchContentPort implementation NO-GO at current HEAD. First decide authentic model ownership, token/fence owner, BookHelp persistence host boundary and exact CoroutineContext propagation. AnalyzeUrl request parity remains NO-GO until its core and Android host effects are separated and reconciled.

### 24.267.1 Task 026CV result — transient model binding plus full per-invocation context (2026-11-28)

- **Identity:** registration HEAD 2ef1808e3594340f1dd23e0b1759598e02d2a965; fixed Legado 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a. Report /tmp/task026cv-model-host-binding/RESULT.md, SHA-256 15fdf7892fd9b296e2d6a1341bba1a1a07f1920fa1847261140fd018f5db8871.
- **Preferred design:** immutable application-scoped Host Port bundle + transient per-object binding on authentic BookSource/Book/BookChapter + explicit full RuntimeExecutionContext per invocation. Binding contains only durable model services; no Activity/View/WebView/Job/CoroutineContext/UI callback. Execution context carries the original CoroutineContext and per-operation state.
- **Why not registries:** BookChapter.equals/hashCode use URL only, Book uses bookUrl and BookSource uses bookSourceUrl; ordinary WeakHashMap keys therefore collide by equality. ThreadLocal is unsafe across coroutine dispatch/WebView callbacks. A wrapper/decorator changes model class/object identity. A global mutable context/service locator creates hidden cross-source state.
- **Lifecycle:** body properties must not enter primary constructors (preserve constructor/componentN/copy/equals/hashCode); exclude binding from Room, Parcelable and Gson/source JSON; reattach after Kotlin copy(), parcel/reload and any future Room materialization. Rebind factory validates source/book/chapter identity.
- **BaseSource:** do not add a new abstract property because BaseSource is also implemented by RssSource, HttpTTS and other upstream types. Use a default nullable getter or BookSource-specific binding; only BookSource receives book-source persistence binding unless caller evidence expands scope.
- **CoroutineContext:** SourceExecutionContext is a host projection with optional Job, not the full execution context. Preserve original CoroutineContext (including SuppressSourceNavigation) through AnalyzeRule→AnalyzeUrl→Rhino→HiddenWebView→callback/login/navigation; do not reconstruct from Job. Existing SourceNavigationBridge captures context and applies both marker and dynamic AppConfig flag.
- **Open gates:** all copy/reload/parcel callsites; exact annotation placement/compile behavior; concurrent source isolation; model methods with no context parameter; SourceNavigationBridge delegated annotation/R8/DEX proof; 026CC data owner and writer; lifecycle/rebind tests.
- **Verification:** static source/API design only. No code/test/Gradle/CI/GitHub/build/device changes. Standing remote-CI authorization remains active for future registered validation tasks; not used here.
- **Disposition:** binding design recommended, implementation NO-GO until rebind/callsite inventory and data-owner acceptance. Phase A OPEN; Stage-0 in_progress / not accepted; Stage-1 NO-GO; Task 027 BLOCKED; full Legado compatibility NOT ESTABLISHED.

### 24.279 Task 026DE result — authentic BookHelp raw-content and token ownership traced (2026-11-28)

- Task 026DE static source investigation completed at pinned Legado SHA 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a. Start HEAD 8c5f4e91370c9fc0c44d23d9642d7a04a028413e; no production source, test, Gradle, schema, workflow or user data changed. Evidence is source inspection only; no upstream Android test/build was run in this task.
- **Upstream data ownership:** Book entity is Room table books with primary key bookUrl (Book.kt:33-43); BookChapter is Room table chapters with composite PK (url,bookUrl), non-unique bookUrl index, unique (bookUrl,index) index, and CASCADE FK to Book (BookChapter.kt:29-42). BookChapter has metadata fields including title, URL, index, VIP/pay flags, resourceUrl, tag, wordCount, offsets/fragments, variable and imgUrl (BookChapter.kt:42-60); its DAO supports index-ordered chapter lookup and independent metadata updates (BookChapterDao.kt:22-53).
- **Raw chapter content owner:** BookHelp uses appCtx.externalFiles as downloadDir, book_cache as root, then Book.getFolderName() and BookChapter.getFileName(); chapter file names are zero-padded index + MD5(title) + .nb (BookHelp.kt:127-138; Book.kt:395-402; BookChapter.kt:195-200). BookHelp.writeText creates that file and calls ordinary File.writeText(content), then removes the .reversed sidecar; for online TXT it separately updates wordCount via BookChapterDao (BookHelp.kt:451-471). This is not the same as Room chapter metadata or the App parsed-content cache.
- **Save token:** ContentSaveKey = (bookUrl,chapterIndex); ContentSaveToken carries that key, folderName and version (BookHelp.kt:59-71, 359-369, 448-449). ContentSaveFence keeps version/fileName in a process-local ConcurrentHashMap and serializes writes with synchronized methods (BookHelp.kt:81-124). writeIfCurrent publishes only if expectedVersion matches; replace advances version before write, even when the write fails. The state is not persisted, so its generation resets with process restart. BookHelp.saveContent validates bookUrl/index/folderName, then executes writeText and optional DAO metadata update inside writeIfCurrent; saveChapterMetadata defaults false; accepted saves post SAVE_CONTENT (BookHelp.kt:238-280). The file write and DAO metadata update are not one cross-store database transaction, and writeText itself is not AtomicFile-backed.
- **Batch lifecycle:** both JS-source and rule-source batch callers capture a token per chapter index before executing the batch (JsSourceBook.kt:150-168; BookContent.kt:283-325). BatchContentContext resolves BookChapter object by index or URL only when URL is unique, rejects ambiguous duplicate-URL strings, applies source replacement, requires the captured token, invokes BookHelp.saveContent, records per-index partial success and refuses callbacks after close (BatchContentContext.kt:31-43, 70-99, 106-118, 121-155). JsExtensions.cacheContent unwraps Rhino Wrapper and delegates to the active batch context; it is unavailable outside batch context (JsExtensions.kt:135-155). Both caller paths close context in finally and return missing chapters for single-chapter fallback. CacheBook.runBatch retains already saved chapters if a later batch script fails and checks captured tokens before publishing reader success (CacheBook.kt:389-432).
- **Other upstream call paths:** CacheBook captures tokens before individual asynchronous chapter work and checks them before UI/result publication (CacheBook.kt:334-357, 454-475, 515-557); ReadBook checks the token before processing and publishing text chapters (ReadBook.kt:1540-1563, 1800-1815). BookHelp.delContent advances the fence before deleting a chapter file (BookHelp.kt:752-765). By contrast, clearCache() and clearCache(book) delete cache directories without enumerating chapters to advance their individual tokens (BookHelp.kt:140-149); whether in-flight operations can repopulate after those clear operations needs a dedicated regression test before claiming invalidation parity.
- **Badcat owner today:** FileChapterContentCache writes under applicationContext.filesDir/legado_chapter_cache, keyed by sourceId + bookUrl + chapter index (legacy URL overload also exists); JSON stores ChapterContent(title,text,nextPageUrl,previousChapterUrl) and savedAt, with chapterUrl as index-keyed entry metadata. It uses AtomicFile, a process-wide Mutex/fence, 4 MiB entry cap and 64 MiB LRU cap (FileChapterContentCache.kt:23-35, 64-94, 96-105, 134-196). SourceChapterContentService captures a token before network fetch, parses pages, applies replacement, stores the final parsed/purified ChapterContent and tolerates cache-write failure without discarding successfully loaded text (SourceChapterContentService.kt:34-49, 112-167). This is explicitly an offline/TTL cache, not the upstream BookHelp source-body file store.
- **Host data boundary:** BadcatReadingStateRepository stores progress/bookmarks in one SharedPreferences file and history JSON in another (BadcatReadingStateRepository.kt:18-23, 44-62, 72-109, 133-176). App source files expose source/replacement catalogs, reading-state repository and parsed chapter cache; no authentic persistent Book/BookChapter repository or BookHelp raw-body owner was found in the App module during this bounded inventory. The engine BookChapter/ChapterContent types are facade DTOs, not upstream Room entities.
- **Gap matrix:** (1) upstream raw file vs Badcat parsed cache — semantic mismatch, NO parity; (2) token key upstream (bookUrl,index) + folderName vs Badcat (sourceId,bookUrl,index) — related but not identical identity; (3) both fences process-local, but upstream raw writer lacks AtomicFile while Badcat parsed cache has AtomicFile; (4) upstream chapter metadata and body are separate stores; Badcat has no chapter metadata repository; (5) upstream batch partial success/missing fallback and late-callback close semantics are not implemented by current Badcat cacheContent bridge, which deliberately throws; (6) cache clear versus in-flight token invalidation remains an upstream test gap.
- **Tests found:** pinned upstream ContentSaveFenceTest covers fence ordering, stale write rejection and metadata source contracts (5 tests); BatchContentContextTest covers URL ambiguity/identity/missing-chapter behavior (10 tests). These are source tests in upstream but were not run by Task 026DE; they do not constitute process-restart durability or cross-store crash-recovery proof.
- **Disposition:** Task 026DE static trace accepted. The required raw BookHelp persistence owner, token/fence semantics and current Badcat mismatch are now evidence-indexed. Do not reuse FileChapterContentCache as raw content, do not construct a shadow Book/BookChapter DTO as a persistence replacement, and do not select Room/file backend from the fixture PoC. Phase A OPEN; Stage-0 not accepted; Stage-1 NO-GO; Task 027 BLOCKED; full compatibility NOT ESTABLISHED.

### 24.292.1 Task 026DK scope expansion — annotated WebView API is not the full Rhino-visible Java surface

- Exact source evidence: BaseSource.evalJS binds the live source object as java/source/sourceApi; JsSourceEngine.buildScope binds its live engine as java and BookSource as source/sourceApi. App.kt registers NativeBaseSource.factory for BookSource, RssSource and HttpTTS. RhinoScriptEngine installs RhinoWrapFactory; the registered wrapper extends CatchableNativeJavaObject -> NativeJavaObject.
- NativeBaseSource overrides has/get only to hide property-style setX aliases when the corresponding property exists (except setVariable), and put only to allow the variable property. It does not filter method names by @JavascriptInterface. Therefore the 68-row 026CS/026DI map is the annotated WebView bridge subset, not the complete public method surface available through the Rhino source object.
- JsExtensions declares many public unannotated methods (ajax/ajaxAll/connect/webView/startBrowserAwait/get/head/post/strToBytes/bytesToStr/readFile/queryTTF/replaceFont/toURL/toast/log/singleFlight/lock/tick/config helpers, etc.). These must be included in the method/overload and Host Port closure where the Rhino wrapper exposes them. JsEncodeUtils also contributes public methods. Do not silently treat @JavascriptInterface as the Rhino exposure gate.
- JS-source execution has a second object surface: JsSourceEngine itself is bound as java; BookSource is bound as source/sourceApi. The default Rhino wrapper is used for JsSourceEngine (no NativeBaseSource registration). This means engine public methods and source public methods are distinct surfaces and require separate compiled/reflection review.
- NativeBaseSource is registered only for BookSource, RssSource and HttpTTS. BookCover's BaseSource implementation is not registered by App.kt and remains a separate product-only/unknown script-wrapper path; do not assume all BaseSource implementors share identical Rhino wrapper semantics.
- Scope amendment: add an exact public-method/overload inventory for BaseSource + JsExtensions + JsEncodeUtils and the JsSourceEngine bound object, mark @JavascriptInterface separately from Rhino-visible/public exposure, and reconcile every method with the 68 annotated map. Reuse the 68 existing rows; only add the previously omitted public non-annotated declarations and wrapper/engine surface. No broad repository scan.
- This is a compatibility-critical finding, not evidence of runtime test or compiled ABI behavior. Static wrapper code proves the intended exposure path; exact runtime reflection/R8/DEX exposure still requires a later separately registered proof task.

- **Upstream model evidence:** pinned BookSource is a Parcelable Room @Entity data class implementing BaseSource; getKey() returns bookSourceUrl, getTag() returns bookSourceName, and equals/hashCode are keyed by bookSourceUrl. One authoritative upstream BookSource/BaseSource/Book/BookChapter object graph must reach Rhino; do not pass app.badcat.engine.BookSource or Map descriptors as the full source object. The custom integration-contract model may remain temporarily for import/test boundaries, not as the Legado runtime object. Book/Chapter identity, RuleData/InfoMap, full CoroutineContext, BatchContentContext and ContentSaveToken remain typed.

DefaultProcessCookieBridge remains test-only; HiddenWebView/browser/CAPTCHA/ProductEvent/BatchContent/SharedJsScope/Reader-Theme-Font production ports remain open. BadcatWebViewPurificationAdapter is visible-page AdMark injection, not HiddenWebViewPort.
- **Required module constraint:** :legado-runtime cannot depend on :app. It already has Android/Parcelize support, but currently lacks Room runtime and several BookSource dependencies (AppPattern, BookSourceType, AudioPlay and converter helpers). Whether App Room KSP can consume an entity defined in :legado-runtime is an explicit compile gate. Keep DAO/repository in App and only one BookSource class/data writer.

## 24.299 Task 026DN result — App-hosted pinned source set selected; Book metadata owner remains open

- **Identity:** start branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; start HEAD \`5ad5729312332216d67d775ae686cf517ed3ccfe\`; fixed Legado SHA \`330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a\`; pinned submodule clean.
- **Import closure:** ten pinned source files (BaseSource, BookSource, Book, BookChapter, AnalyzeRule, AnalyzeUrl, JsExtensions, JsEncodeUtils, JsSourceEngine, SharedJsScope) contain 386 direct imports. Classification: 170 App host/product; 37 Android/Room/Parcelable; 50 other external/static; 41 JDK/Kotlin; 23 third-party; 21 upstream runtime model; 19 upstream model; 15 coroutines; eight unresolved upstream App package; two Android product UI/media. Per-file counts: 31/20/29/25/54/71/94/9/27/26 respectively.
- **Placement decision:** compile the exact pinned upstream model/execution classes in an App-hosted pinned source set under original FQCNs. :app already depends on :legado-runtime and :legado-rhino and owns the App services those files import. :legado-runtime remains typed HostPort contracts + its seven already-compiled upstream rule models/GsonExtensions; :legado-rhino remains Rhino; :integration-contract remains transitional custom DTO/test contract; :legado-runtime-poc remains quarantined and is not an App dependency. Do not create a :legado-runtime -> :app dependency.
- **Why not move the whole core into :legado-runtime:** BaseSource directly uses AppConfig/CookieStore/CacheManager/ConcurrentRateLimiter/SharedJsScope; Book and BookChapter call appDb and App helpers; AnalyzeUrl imports Cronet/BackstageWebView/CookieManager/Glide/Media3; JsExtensions imports EventBus/Activity/dialog/archive/file/UI. Moving these as-is would create a cycle or require changing concrete model descriptors.
- **Compile gates:** upstream BookSource/Book/BookChapter use Parcelize and Room annotations. Current :app has no kotlin-parcelize plugin, Room runtime/KSP or RoomDatabase. :legado-runtime has Parcelize but no Room runtime; :legado-runtime-poc has Room/Parcelize but is not consumed by :app. App source placement needs Parcelize + Room runtime annotations. Room KSP is only needed if an App Room DB/DAO is chosen. Upstream Book/BookChapter also call appDb; no appDb/RoomDatabase exists in current app/src/main, so those calls must be replaced by App repository ports.
- **Current single-writer state:** FileBookSourceCatalog is the only source-record writer (AtomicFile + process-wide Mutex; LegadoBookSourceCodec retains unknown raw JSON fields) but returns custom app.badcat.engine.BookSource. ## 24.301 Task 026DO result — Room metadata + generation-file content commit protocol defined

- **Identity:** start branch integration/legado-upstream-runtime; start HEAD 101370d748bebceba83fec38b71e56f90caf852b; fixed Legado SHA 330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a; pinned submodule clean.
- **Upstream contract:** ContentSaveToken captures (bookUrl, chapterIndex), book folderName and in-memory version. ContentSaveFence is synchronized/process-local; writeIfCurrent gates publication; replace increments version even on failed writes. BookHelp.saveContent validates bookUrl/index/folder, writes under the fence, optionally updates appDb.bookChapterDao metadata and posts SAVE_CONTENT only after success.
- **Batch contract:** BatchContentContext holds exact BookSource/Book/List<BookChapter>, full CoroutineContext and a per-index token snapshot. It identifies chapters by index; a BookChapter object resolves by index; URL is accepted only when unique; duplicate URL is ambiguous; numeric identifiers are rejected. It applies replaceRegex/online-TXT formatting, checks ensureActive, calls BookHelp.saveContent, closes in finally and returns missing chapters for single-chapter fallback.
- **Current App contract:** ChapterContentSaveToken is (sourceId,bookUrl,chapterIndex,version); ChapterContentSaveFence is process-wide but in-memory. FileChapterContentCache uses AtomicFile, a process-wide Mutex/fence, private filesDir, 4 MiB per-entry and 64 MiB total limits, and stores chapterUrl/title/text/pagination/savedAt. SourceChapterContentService captures a token before network work and only publishes while current; it supports single-chapter pagination but not batch.
- **Critical mismatch:** custom token has sourceId but no folderName/chapterUrl/durable generation; upstream token has folderName but no sourceId. Both versions are process-local. Upstream optionally updates BookChapter metadata and emits SAVE_CONTENT; custom cache stores content only. Upstream path is externalFiles/book_cache; Badcat path is private internal filesDir. Keep the private bounded path.
- **Selected design:** App owns one Room metadata DB/DAO layer for Book and BookChapter metadata/TOC; FileBookSourceCatalog remains the only source-record writer; FileChapterContentCache remains the private raw-content file adapter. Add ContentCommitJournal + ChapterContentRecord keyed by sourceId/bookUrl/chapterIndex. Use immutable generation-specific AtomicFile content files and one App ContentCommitCoordinator; no caller writes around it.
- **Commit protocol:** snapshot upstream token + durable generation; insert PREPARED journal; stage/verify a new generation file; in one Room transaction recheck expected generation, update BookChapter metadata and active file pointer/hash/generation, mark journal COMMITTED; only then publish SAVE_CONTENT/UI events; cleanup old files idempotently. A stale token cannot replace the active pointer. Room metadata failure leaves the old file/pointer current.
- **Crash recovery:** PREPARED without valid file rolls back; staged file without journal is an orphan swept after a grace period; valid staged file with PREPARED journal is completed or rolled back only after generation recheck; COMMITTED journal verifies active hash and cleans old files. Generation-specific files prevent a new write from destroying the old content before DB commit.
- **Batch contract:** wire the real upstream BatchContentContext; preserve object/index identity, duplicate-URL rejection, per-chapter request-start token snapshot, full CoroutineContext cancellation, missing-chapter fallback, close/late-callback rejection and event-after-commit ordering. Do not keep the custom cacheContent throwing stub.
- **Migration:** keep FileBookSourceCatalog raw JSON/unknown fields; migrate both legacy URL-keyed and index-keyed cache files idempotently; validate chapterUrl; do not delete old cache until the new Room pointer commits and a recovery grace period passes. Book/TOC metadata currently has no durable owner, so establish Room owner before migration.
- **Tests inspected (not run):** ChapterContentSaveFenceTest 7; FileChapterContentCacheTest 7; FileChapterContentCacheAtomicFileTest 4. No upstream BatchContentContext test suite was found in the current repository. Failure-injection matrix defines 17 additional cases.
- **Artifacts:** /tmp/task026do-book-chapter-transaction/. upstream-content-save-contract.tsv SHA-256 49a7d1499856c4493620586d49bcdf18a525703d18124ac5205ee92a5685cba6; custom-content-save-contract.tsv ed3681886272e4b82b31b5940bec90aa2d7409289e79667f15accfe20d0983e7; token-and-transaction-diff.tsv aaf5a6b7e5e4debfb08e93cd9b90cc4847b5043b626078442542506cda4426be; batch-content-lifecycle.tsv 9405e7b428f3b06ddf03bec920d08b47fc773a03db40a1984e406c46957a0a62; content-commit-protocol.tsv 4ee94da0e793b399c62b1b983fc7e0001494029989da1a4451d7e30ff7af02f8; crash-recovery-matrix.tsv d4aa5a16138752aef440004db7e42e39966f395dbb4e7fbe0aab2d09dbf1e25b; failure-injection-test-matrix.tsv 8b2e32d38c3b9685a1d6bf2a371d2921ad37dbff2b68a56c83d4926c9c9eb583; migration-compatibility-plan.tsv a7f54b131fe615fb56dc4626e072d9ea9caeab5ac05683711ea20d59b1eb0c4c; SOURCE-SHA256SUMS (16 files) 78700ac79f145db3577f5adb0ad12202e477c6e801678d3bb69b696ee0ed38d2; INPUT-SHA256SUMS (six files) f123aba0cbb223bbfe22cf7cfc9fb781d48451dc214ef7fb633ff542ac3bed96; RESULT.md 022d7450be3364f6498497b6b3a6e7558747de3e25c57507c4fdbe69239a414d; OUTPUT-SHA256SUMS ee0d19adab47758cc26f98d6f86ff88d4b113a2e3a8a8c7bce88615e9faddb69.
